articles.title: VÍDEO: Polícia resgata menina de 2 anos em lago após mãe acionar emergência nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Criança foi encontrada depois de a mãe acionar o serviço de emergência. Ela não apresentava ferimentos aparentes e foi entregue novamente à família.
articles.summary: Criança foi encontrada depois de a mãe acionar o serviço de emergência. Ela não apresentava ferimentos aparentes e foi entregue novamente à família.
articles.body:
Uma menina de 2 anos foi encontrada dentro de um lago e resgatada por policiais minutos depois de a mãe ligar para o serviço de emergência para informar seu desaparecimento. O caso aconteceu na última segunda-feira (16), no condado de Hillsborough, na Flórida, nos Estados Unidos .

Policiais do gabinete do xerife local foram enviados ao endereço informado pela mãe às 13h, no horário local.

As equipes iniciaram as buscas imediatamente e encontraram a criança em um lago próximo sete minutos depois.

A menina foi retirada da água e não apresentava ferimentos aparentes. Ela foi examinada por uma equipe de resgate do Corpo de Bombeiros do condado antes de ser entregue novamente à mãe.

"O que poderia ter sido uma tragédia terminou com essa criança reunida à família", afirmou o xerife Chad Chronister, em publicação no X (ex-Twitter).

articles.title: Presídio de Alfenas: Estado deve comprovar limite de ocupação | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão determina que unidade não ultrapasse 180% da capacidade. OAB afirma que superlotação afeta direitos dos presos, saúde pública e segurança da população.
articles.summary: A Justiça de Minas Gerais deu 15 dias para o Estado comprovar o limite de ocupação no presídio de Alfenas, sob pena de multa diária de R$ 20 mil por superlotação.
articles.body:
A Justiça de Minas Gerais determinou que o Estado comprove, em até 15 dias, que está cumprindo o limite de ocupação estabelecido para o presídio de Alfenas (MG). Em caso de descumprimento, a multa diária prevista é de R$ 20 mil.

Segundo a decisão, a capacidade da unidade não pode ultrapassar 180% da lotação. O Estado foi intimado a informar a capacidade do presídio, o número de leitos existentes acima do chão, a população carcerária atual, o percentual de ocupação e as medidas adotadas para evitar a superlotação.

O presidente da OAB de Alfenas, Gustavo Pérez Barbosa, afirmou que a entidade acompanha a situação há mais tempo do que a própria ação civil pública, proposta em 2017.

Justiça dá 15 dias para Estado comprovar limite de ocupação no presídio de Alfenas sob pena de multa diária de R$ 20 mil — Foto: EPTV/Reprodução

"Na verdade, a OAB acompanha esse problema há um pouco mais de tempo. Nós acompanhamos o problema da superlotação carcerária de Alfenas desde antes de 2017, que é o marco da propositura dessa ação civil pública que hoje está sendo repercutida", afirmou.

De acordo com o presidente da OAB, inspeções realizadas pelas comissões de Assuntos Penitenciários e de Direitos Humanos identificaram problemas relacionados à violação de direitos humanos e à falta de acesso adequado a serviços básicos.

"Os principais problemas estão relacionados, primeiro, à violação de direitos humanos, que é recorrente, à inobservância de direitos mínimos do preso, do preso que perde a liberdade, mas não perde a dignidade. E um outro problema sério diz respeito às condições de saúde, assistência à saúde, assistência social e também assistência jurídica", disse.

Sobre a resposta aguardada do Estado, Gustavo Pérez Barbosa afirmou esperar transparência na apresentação dos dados.

"Nós esperamos que o Estado seja, de fato, transparente e traga os números reais. A gente sabe que o presídio funciona com uma superpopulação, já foi maior, inclusive, mas uma superpopulação. A gente sabe que esse problema não é de Alfenas, é um problema geral. E o que a gente espera do Estado agora, compelido a cumprir uma sentença que limita a lotação do presídio, é que ele, de fato, traga os números reais e que queira, efetivamente, cuidar desse problema", declarou.

O advogado também ressaltou que os impactos da superlotação ultrapassam os muros da unidade prisional.

"Efetivamente, é um problema que afeta não só quem está lá, não só as famílias de quem está lá, mas principalmente nós que estamos aqui fora. Evidentemente que a inobservância de direitos mínimos do preso gera neles e nas famílias um sentimento de revolta. E a revolta aqui fora pode se transformar em violência. Além disso, a disseminação de doenças naquele local é muito fácil, é muito facilitada. E isso desemboca onde? No posto de saúde, no hospital municipal e isso afeta diretamente a vida de quem está aqui fora", afirmou.

Questionado sobre os prazos para a prestação das informações, o presidente da OAB explicou que o Estado foi intimado por meio da Advocacia-Geral do Estado.

"O Estado foi intimado por meio da Advocacia Geral do Estado para fornecer essas informações em tempo hábil. Essa intimação, pelo que eu pude ver, já foi efetivada. O Estado tem prazo em dobro para apresentar essas informações. São informações básicas, não são informações que demandam muito tempo. Mas a gente imagina que o Estado vai gastar todo o tempo necessário e possível para apresentar essas informações", disse.

Em nota enviada à produção da EPTV , a Secretaria de Justiça e Segurança Pública (Sejusp) informou que o presídio de Alfenas possui atualmente 510 vagas. Segundo a pasta, o número exato de presos não pode ser divulgado por questão de segurança.

A Sejusp informou ainda que trabalha para criar 2.700 novas vagas no sistema prisional mineiro por meio da construção e ampliação de unidades, além de parcerias com prefeituras e com o Poder Judiciário para melhorar a estrutura das unidades prisionais.

O Ministério Público também foi procurado para comentar o assunto, mas não disponibilizou representante para entrevista. A instituição informou que o promotor responsável tinha audiências previamente agendadas.

articles.title: Influenciadora Vera Dijkmans é detida pelo ICE nos EUA  | G1
articles.standfirst: Vera Dijkmans, de 29 anos, foi presa ao chegar ao aeroporto de Newark, em Nova Jersey. Segundo o governo americano, ela não compareceu a uma audiência de imigração. A informação foi divulgada por veículos holandeses e americanos.
articles.summary: Vera Dijkmans, de 29 anos, foi presa no dia 11 de novembro. A informação foi divulgada por veículos de notícias holandeses e americanos.
articles.body:
Influenciadora holandesa com mais de 5 milhões de seguidores é detida pelo ICE nos EUA — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

A criadora de conteúdo holandesa Vera Dijkmans, de 29 anos, está detida pelo Serviço de Imigração e Controle de Alfândegas dos Estados Unidos (ICE). A informação foi divulgada por veículos de notícias holandeses e americanos.

Segundo relatos, a influenciadora foi detida em 11 de novembro, ao desembarcar no Aeroporto Internacional de Newark, em Nova Jersey. Ela havia chegado em um voo procedente de Miami.

Dijkmans tem mais de 5 milhões de seguidores no Instagram e também mantém um perfil no OnlyFans, plataforma de conteúdo adulto.

O Departamento de Segurança Interna dos Estados Unidos (DHS) informou à a emissora pública holandesa NOS que Vera foi detida porque não compareceu a uma audiência no tribunal de imigração, realizada em maio.

O órgão também afirmou que ela permaneceu no país além do período autorizado pelo visto. De acordo com a emissora regional holandesa Omroep Brabant, a influenciadora já é alvo de um processo de deportação, mas ainda não há uma data definida para sua saída dos Estados Unidos.

A família afirma que Vera estava no país com um visto de turista (B-2). Em entrevista à RTL Nieuws, a mãe dela, Marianne Scholt, disse que a filha perdeu a audiência porque estava viajando.

Segundo o jornal americano New York Post, Vera está em um centro de detenção em Nova Jersey. Familiares relataram ao jornal que ela enfrenta condições precárias no local.

De acordo com os relatos, a influenciadora divide o espaço com outras 12 pessoas e passou vários dias sem ter acesso à luz do sol. As informações sobre as condições de detenção foram atribuídas à família e não foram confirmadas de forma independente.

Até a publicação desta reportagem, não havia manifestação pública da defesa da influenciadora.

Natural de Waalwijk, no sul dos Países Baixos, Vera ganhou projeção internacional em 2023, quando passou a se apresentar como a "namorada mais desejada do mundo".

No Instagram, ela publica fotos e vídeos sobre diferentes assuntos, incluindo artes marciais. A influenciadora também mantém um perfil no OnlyFans.

articles.title: Filho do vice-governador do Piauí recebe bênção do Papa no Vaticano | G1
articles.standfirst: O momento foi registrado durante uma saudação do Papa aos fiéis no Vaticano. Ao passar pelo local, ele abençoa Pedro Victor e outras crianças presentes.
articles.summary: Filho do vice-governador do Piauí recebeu a bênção do Papa Leão XIV na Praça São Pedro, no Vaticano, uma semana antes de completar seu primeiro ano de vida.
articles.body:
O vice-governador eleito do Piauí, Washington Bandeira Filho, compartilhou nas redes sociais, nesta quarta-feira (18), um momento em que o filho, Pedro Victor, recebeu uma bênção do Papa Leão XIV, na Praça São Pedro, no Vaticano. Segundo ele, a criança completa 1 ano na próxima semana.

Na postagem, Washington descreveu o momento como uma experiência marcante para a família.

"Um dia que ficará guardado pra sempre na nossa memória e no nosso coração. Uma emoção única para mim e Fernanda. Obrigado por esta glória para a nossa família, meu Deus!," escreveu.

O registro aconteceu durante uma saudação do Papa aos fiéis na praça. Nas imagens, ele passa pelo local em um veículo utilizado para cumprimentar os presentes e abençoar crianças. Em seguida, uma das pessoas que acompanha o carro leva Pedro Victor até o Papa e ele estende a mão sobre a criança e concede a bênção.

Após a bênção, Washington Bandeira e a esposa, Fernanda Negrão, abraçam o filho emocionados.

Papa Leão XIV abençoa filho do vice-governador eleito do Piauí, no Vaticano. — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: Planeta Atlântida 2027: Anitta, Luan Santana e line-up completo | G1
articles.standfirst: Atrações como Luan Santana, Anitta, Pedro Sampaio, Jorge & Mateus e Thiaguinho estão confirmadas no festival, que ocorre nos dias 29 e 30 de janeiro, em Atlântida
articles.summary: O Planeta Atlântida 2027 confirmou Anitta, Luan Santana e Jorge & Mateus em um line-up diverso que agitará o litoral gaúcho nos dias 29 e 30 de janeiro.
articles.body:
Mantendo a tradição de ser palco para diferentes gêneros musicais, o Planeta Atlântida divulgou, nesta quarta-feira (18), o line-up da edição de 2027 , que será realizada nos dias 29 e 30 de janeiro , em Atlântida, no Litoral gaúcho.

Entre os artistas confirmados estão nomes como Anitta , Luan Santana , Pedro Sampaio, Jorge e Mateus e Thiaguinho. Marcado pela diversidade, o maior festival de música do sul do país vai do pop ao sertanejo, do rap ao funk, passando por pagode, rock, reggae e eletrônico, em uma mistura eclética e única.

Pelo segundo ano consecutivo, Anitta carimba o passaporte para o Planeta. Em 2026, a poderosa lançou dois álbuns conceituais e conquistou pela primeira vez um Grammy Latino — após ser indicada 12 vezes na disputa, abocanhou o prêmio de Melhor Álbum de Pop Contemporâneo em Língua Portuguesa com Equilibrivm. Para 2027, a cantora ganha ainda mais relevância internacional ao concorrer com o mesmo disco ao Grammy na categoria Melhor Álbum de Música Global.

Outro artista que tem conquistado cada vez mais espaço fora do Brasil, Pedro Sampaio volta ao Planeta Atlântida para agitar o público com sucessos do naipe de Joga Pra Lua, POCPOC e Perversa — música em parceria com o colombiano JBalvin.

Ainda na batida do funk, os planetários também podem aproveitar o som do DJ, produtor e compositor Dennis, que integrou o time da Furacão 2000 e produziu alguns dos maiores hits do funk carioca, como Cerol na Mão e Um Tapinha Não Dói.

Quem gosta da pista de dança também vai aproveitar o show do Baile Lotadão, projeto itinerante do DJ e produtor Victor Lou em parceria com o DJ GBR, que transita por vertentes como house, techno, bass e funk, e do gaúcho Ariel B, conhecido dos planetários que agita o público com sua mistura de funk e música eletrônica.

Dois fenômenos do sertanejo retornam ao Planeta em 2027. Quatro anos depois de seu último show na Saba, Luan Santana chega com hits da turnê Registro Histórico, que foi recorde de bilheteria em todo o Brasil e faz um apanhado da carreira do músico com faixas como Te Esperando e Escreve Aí.

O time do modão é reforçado com os goianos Jorge & Mateus, que se apresentaram pela última vez no festival em 2014. A dupla é conhecida por algumas das levadas mais animadas do sertanejo universitário, como Pode Chorar e Voa Beija-Flor.

O pagode também ganha espaço no Planeta 2027 com nomes de peso. Indicado quatro vezes ao Grammy Latino, Thiaguinho lançou neste ano Bem Black, o 24º disco de sua carreira. Péricles e Ferrugem levam para a Saba o espetáculo As Vozes, que junta duas gerações do samba e pagode em um só palco.

Seguindo a trilha dos ritmos nacionais, Dominguinho – projeto que venceu o Grammy Latino na categoria Melhor Álbum de Música de Raízes em Língua Portuguesa em 2025 e 2026 e que arrasta multidões em todo o país –, traz a união do cantor João Gomes com o vocalista e violonista Jota.pê e o sanfoneiro Mestrinho.

Os graves do trap e do rap vão ecoar pela Saba com BK, que conquistou o Prêmio da Música Brasileira na categoria Melhor Artista de Rap/Trap e tornou-se o primeiro rapper brasileiro a realizar um show solo no Nubank Parque, em São Paulo.

As rimas também ganham voz com Veigh, fenômeno de audiência; Duquesa, que em 2026 foi um dos maiores destaques no Tiny Desk Brasil; Teto, destaque da nova geração do trap nacional; Alee, que já se apresentou no Lollapalooza Brasil e no The Town; e a combinação do funk paulista de MC IG (que lançou em 2025 o álbum Quem Tá Vivo, Tá Vivendo) com a participação do gaúcho DJ Gabriel R.

Ritmo que não pode faltar, o pop aparece em diferentes roupagens no line-up do Planeta 2027. Uma das principais forças do pop nacional contemporâneo, Jão chega à Saba depois de uma conquista recente: foi o primeiro artista solo a esgotar três datas no Allianz Parque.

Atração da primeira semana de novembro do Tiny Desk Brasil, Marina Sena desembarca pela primeira vez na Saba com seu som autêntico, resultado da envolvente mistura de samba, reggae, axé, MPB e dancehall. Sucesso que nasceu em Caxias do Sul e ganhou o Brasil, Syon Trio volta ao Planeta após se apresentar no Lollapalooza e no Grande Prêmio de São Paulo de Fórmula 1 de 2026.

Os mineiros da Lagum trazem mais uma vez ao Planeta o seu pop rock com ecos de MPB e reggae. Na pegada mais rock’n’roll, o destaque vai para a Fresno, que em 2026 fez o maior show de sua história no Parque da Redenção, em Porto Alegre. Os gaúchos se apresentam no Planeta contando com a participação de Di Ferrero (NX Zero).

Outro expoente do rock nacional que despontou nos anos 2000 e está na escalação é CPM22. A banda volta ao Planeta depois de sete anos celebrando mais de três décadas de história e cinco indicações ao Grammy Latino.

Trio formado por José Gil, Francisco Gil e João Gil – respectivamente filho e netos de Gilberto Gil -, a banda Gilsons combina MPB, samba, pop, ritmos afro-baianos, afoxé, hip-hop e elementos eletrônicos.

Quem também carrega no sangue a herança da boa música é Chico Chico: filho de Cássia Eller, o músico lançou em 2025 Let It Burn /Deixa Arder, álbum que mistura rock, blues, folk, milonga e diferentes ritmos brasileiros.

Estrela da campanha publicitária do Planeta Atlântida 2027, o poeta Armandinho tem seu 18º encontro marcado com os planetários, quando faz mais um show inesquecível – “pra sempre ou só por um momento”, como diz o trecho da música Outra Noite Que Se Vai, que é o conceito desta edição do festival. E, como já é tradição, Neto Fagundes dará as boas-vindas ao público.

Depois de uma edição histórica de 30 anos, o Planeta Atlântida segue reafirmando sua capacidade de se reinventar e conectar diferentes gerações por meio da música. Nossa essência está na diversidade de estilos e na pluralidade de encontros que fazem do festival um reflexo da cultura e do comportamento do público. Seguimos olhando para a frente, em busca de novas possibilidades, sem perder o que nos torna tão especiais: a capacidade de criar momentos que ficam para sempre na memória de quem faz parte dessa história", destaca Gustavo Sirotsky, diretor artístico do Planeta Atlântida.

Os ingressos para o Planeta Atlântida 2027 estão disponíveis no site planetaatlantida.com.br e nas Lojas Renner dos shoppings Iguatemi e Praia de Belas, em Porto Alegre. O evento respeita a classificação etária. Menores de 14 anos não poderão entrar, mesmo acompanhados dos pais ou responsáveis legais.

articles.title: Toyota do Brasil apresenta a Corolla Deck; picape tem motor híbrido flex e chega em 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova linha de produção montará também o sedã Corolla, que deixou de ser fabricado em Indaiatuba (SP). Picape será exportada para mercados da América Latina.
articles.summary: Nova linha de produção montará também o sedã Corolla, que deixou de ser fabricado em Indaiatuba (SP). Picape será exportada para mercados da América Latina.
articles.body:
Toyota Corolla Deck. — Foto: Divulgação / Toyota

A Toyota anunciou nesta quarta-feira (18) a Corolla Deck, picape híbrida flex da família Corolla que será vendida exclusivamente na América Latina.

A produção está prevista para o primeiro semestre de 2027 na nova fábrica de Sorocaba (SP), inaugurada durante a cerimônia em que a marca confirmou o modelo.

A engenharia local participou do desenvolvimento da picape. Segundo a Toyota, a proposta é oferecer o conforto e a dirigibilidade de um SUV para o uso na cidade e em viagens em família.

A marca diz ter priorizado a estabilidade e as reações previsíveis ao volante, tanto nas ruas quanto nas estradas.

A caçamba terá tampa traseira amortecida e altura que facilita o carregamento. Na cabine, o projeto deu atenção ao espaço e à posição de quem viaja no banco traseiro, além de facilitar a entrada e a saída dos passageiros.

A Toyota afirma que o sistema híbrido flex ajuda a reduzir o consumo de combustível e as emissões de CO₂.

A estreia está prevista para 2027, ainda sem data definida. A marca vai divulgar os preços, as condições de venda e mais detalhes da picape no lançamento.

Toyota apresenta picape híbrida Corolla Deck. — Foto: Carlos Cereijo / g1

A Corolla Deck será o primeiro modelo inédito da fábrica Sorocaba 2. A unidade começa a operar com o Corolla sedã, cuja produção foi transferida de Indaiatuba (SP).

Com capacidade inicial para fabricar 100 mil veículos por ano, a nova planta eleva para 270 mil unidades anuais a capacidade de produção da Toyota no Brasil.

A fábrica tem 160 mil m² de área construída e faz parte do investimento de R$ 11,5 bilhões anunciado pela Toyota em 2024.

A operação começa com 1.700 empregos diretos, e a previsão é chegar a 2.000 até 2030. As mulheres representam 50% das contratações.

Toyota mostra nova picape Corolla Deck. — Foto: Carlos Cereijo / g1

Com a chegada da picape, o complexo de Sorocaba reunirá a produção de cinco modelos. Além do sedã e da Corolla Deck na nova unidade, a fábrica Sorocaba 1 produz os SUVs Corolla Cross e Yaris Cross e o Yaris hatch, destinado exclusivamente à exportação.

Na nova linha, robôs executam 99,5% das operações de soldagem das carrocerias. Segundo a Toyota, a fábrica consome 52% menos água e emite cerca de 42% menos CO₂ por veículo produzido em comparação com a unidade de Indaiatuba.

Nova picape da Toyota usa base do Corolla Cross. — Foto: Divulgação / Toyota

articles.title: Sarna humana em MS: creche fecha em Campo Grande e casos sobem | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Secretaria de Educação, Campo Grande não está em situação de surto de sarna humana, apesar da investigação de outras três suspeitas. Em Mato Grosso do Sul, os registros já chegam a 117 em cinco municípios da região sul do estado.
articles.summary: A EMEI Jasmim Ibrahim Bacha suspendeu aulas para sanitização após caso de sarna humana, enquanto Mato Grosso do Sul soma 117 registros da doença em cinco cidades.
articles.body:
A Escola Municipal de Educação Infantil (EMEI) Jasmim Ibrahim Bacha, no bairro Nova Lima, foi fechada nesta quarta-feira (18), em Campo Grande, após a confirmação de um caso de sarna humana. A suspensão das aulas foi necessária para a sanitização do espaço.

A Secretaria Municipal de Saúde (Sesau) investiga outros três casos suspeitos da doença na capital. Em todo o ano passado, foram registrados três casos de sarna humana em Campo Grande, segundo a pasta. A prefeitura afirma que não há surto confirmado na cidade neste ano. Os casos suspeitos são acompanhados pela Vigilância em Saúde.

Em Mato Grosso do Sul, porém, o cenário é diferente: pelo menos 117 casos foram registrados em cinco municípios neste mês. Além de Campo Grande, há registros em: Dourados, Itaporã, Amambai, Nova Andradina e Douradina.

🔎A sarna humana, também chamada de escabiose, é causada por um ácaro que provoca coceira intensa, principalmente à noite. A doença também pode causar pequenas lesões e marcas avermelhadas na pele.

🔎🔎A transmissão ocorre principalmente pelo contato direto e prolongado com a pele de uma pessoa infectada. O compartilhamento de roupas, toalhas e roupas de cama usadas recentemente também pode transmitir o ácaro.

Emei fechada em Campo Grande. — Foto: Emilenne Queiroz/g1 MS

Os primeiros casos foram identificados em Itaporã e Dourados. Nesta terça-feira (17), Nova Andradina também confirmou quatro registros. Juntas, as três cidades somam pelo menos 112 casos da doença.

As secretarias municipais de Saúde ainda não identificaram o que provocou o aumento de casos. Enquanto isso, reforçam as orientações de prevenção para moradores, especialmente crianças, que estão entre os grupos mais afetados.

A Prefeitura de Nova Andradina intensificou o monitoramento e as ações de prevenção contra a sarna humana. As equipes de saúde acompanham os casos confirmados, investigam suspeitas, avaliam pacientes e oferecem tratamento.

As equipes também identificam e orientam as pessoas que moram com os pacientes. Quando necessário, os contatos próximos recebem tratamento ao mesmo tempo. A prefeitura ainda reforça as orientações sobre sintomas, transmissão e prevenção.

Em Dourados e Itaporã, cidades vizinhas, as aulas foram suspensas em unidades de ensino que registraram casos da doença. Juntas, as duas cidades somam pelo menos 108 infecções.

Em Itaporã, as aulas no Centro Municipal de Educação Infantil (CMEI) Milton Menani foram retomadas nesta segunda-feira (16), após oito dias de suspensão por causa de um surto de sarna humana que atingiu crianças e funcionários da unidade.

Outra unidade, o CMEI Maria Rodrigues Dias, também registrou sete casos da doença. A previsão é que as aulas sejam retomadas nesta quarta-feira (18).

Em Dourados, os casos mais recentes foram registrados na Escola Municipal Franklin Luiz Azambuja, no bairro BNH IV Plano. A unidade tem 13 casos confirmados: 12 entre alunos e um entre professores. Apesar dos registros, as aulas continuam normalmente.

Apesar das notificações feitas pela escola e dos atestados apresentados por pais de alunos e por uma funcionária, a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde ainda considera os casos suspeitos.

Quais são os sintomas e quando procurar atendimento?

Entre os principais sinais da escabiose estão a coceira intensa, que costuma piorar à noite, e o aparecimento de lesões na pele.

A orientação da Sesau é que pessoas com esses sintomas procurem uma Unidade de Saúde da Família (USF) para avaliação e tratamento adequado.

Os contatos próximos de pessoas infectadas também devem ser avaliados por profissionais de saúde, mesmo que ainda não apresentem sintomas.

Para reduzir o risco de transmissão, a Sesau recomenda reforçar os cuidados com a higiene pessoal e dos ambientes. Entre as medidas estão:

Lavar e higienizar roupas, toalhas e roupas de cama;

Limpar superfícies e materiais de uso coletivo;

Evitar compartilhar objetos de uso pessoal;

Procurar atendimento médico ao apresentar sintomas;

Orientar e avaliar pessoas que tiveram contato próximo com alguém infectado.

Em instituições de ensino, a orientação da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde é comunicar os responsáveis, acompanhar os casos e reforçar as medidas de higiene, sempre preservando a privacidade das pessoas acometidas.

O afastamento temporário de alunos ou funcionários deve considerar a avaliação clínica e o início do tratamento adequado.

A suspensão das atividades escolares não é automática. A necessidade de fechar uma escola ou creche deve ser avaliada em conjunto pelas autoridades sanitárias e educacionais, de acordo com as características de cada situação.

articles.title: In 2000, Roger Daltrey helped launch a concert series for teenagers with cancer; 26 years later, 150 Royal Albert Hall shows have raised more than £36 million to support their care
articles.summary: A concert series that began with a simple idea of bringing music and support together for young people with cancer has grown into one of Britain's most
articles.body: A concert series that began with a simple idea of bringing music and support together for young people with cancer has grown into one of Britain's most successful charity fundraising events. More than two decades after Roger Daltrey helped launch the initiative, the Teenage Cancer Trust has reached a milestone of 150 shows at London's Royal Albert Hall, raising over £36 million for specialist cancer care and support.According to an announcement published by the Teenage Cancer Trust on March 27, 2026, the milestone was reached during the charity's annual concert series, which began in 2000. Over the years, hundreds of musicians and performers have volunteered their time, helping the organisation fund specialist nursing care, youth support services and age-appropriate hospital environments for young people undergoing cancer treatment.How Roger Daltrey started the concert seriesThe initiative was founded by Sir Roger Daltrey, the lead singer of British rock band The Who, who wanted to use the music industry's influence to support teenagers and young adults diagnosed with cancer. The inaugural concert took place at the Royal Albert Hall in November 2000, with Daltrey and his band joined on stage by musicians including Noel Gallagher, Bryan Adams, Paul Weller, Eddie Vedder, Nigel Kennedy and Kelly Jones.Daltrey believed that music offered an opportunity to bring together artists and audiences for a cause that directly affected young people. Speaking about the original idea, he highlighted how much the music industry owed to teenagers, whose enthusiasm had helped shape rock and roll. The concerts gradually became an annual fundraising event, attracting some of the biggest names in music and comedy. According to the charity, more than 500 artists have donated their time and talent since the series began.Performers who have appeared at the Royal Albert Hall shows over the years include Paul McCartney, Oasis, The Who and Kasabian, alongside numerous other established and emerging artists.150 shows and more than £36 million raisedThe 150th show took place in March 2026, when Manic Street Preachers performed at the Royal Albert Hall. The year's programme was curated by Robert Smith of The Cure and also featured artists including Elbow, Mogwai, My Bloody Valentine, Garbage and Placebo. The milestone reflects the scale of the fundraising effort built around the concerts. The more than £36 million raised has helped Teenage Cancer Trust provide specialist nursing care, expert youth support and hospital environments designed around the needs of young patients.The charity has also highlighted the wider reach of the initiative. Its Royal Albert Hall concerts have sold more than 500,000 tickets and generated funding equivalent to over a million hours of specialist care, according to figures shared when Daltrey stepped down from leading the concert series in 2024. In 2017, the event celebrated another major milestone when it reached 100 Royal Albert Hall shows. The Who, the band that helped launch the original concerts, returned to perform that year.Daltrey's contribution recognised with a knighthoodDaltrey's involvement with Teenage Cancer Trust extended well beyond organising concerts. He was the driving force behind the annual fundraising shows for more than two decades and continues to support the organisation as its Honorary Patron. In June 2025, he received a knighthood in King Charles III's Birthday Honours for his services to charity. The Teenage Cancer Trust congratulated him, recognising his contribution to raising funds and improving support for young people with cancer.At the time, Daltrey said he accepted the honour on behalf of the many people who had helped make the charity successful. He also acknowledged the contribution of The Who, its fans and the individuals who had supported the organisation over the years. The charity said the concerts had helped it develop a network of 28 specialist units in NHS hospitals across the UK.Why specialist cancer care matters for teenagersTeenage Cancer Trust focuses on the particular needs of young people aged 13 to 24, whose experiences of cancer treatment can differ from those of children and older adults. The organisation says seven young people in the UK receive a cancer diagnosis every day. Its work includes providing specialist nurses, support teams and hospital environments that help patients maintain a sense of normality during treatment. The charity also highlights gaps in cancer services, including access to mental health support, timely diagnosis and clinical trials.For Daltrey, the 150-show milestone represents the collective contribution of musicians, audiences, organisers and supporters who have helped sustain the initiative since 2000. What began as a series of charity concerts has developed into a long-running fundraising effort, with its impact extending beyond the stage and into specialist care for thousands of young people.You use AI every day. articles.title: China switched on a battery the size of a building that stores power in tanks of liquid electrolyte; less flammable, designed for repeated charging, and able to meet the daily electricity needs of 200,000 people
articles.summary: Discover China's groundbreaking vanadium flow battery in Dalian, a massive energy storage facility that powers 200,000 residents. Learn about its technology, benefits, and the future of renewable energy storage.
articles.body: In 2022, China brought a large energy storage facility online in the northeastern city of Dalian. Often described as a giant power bank, it stores electricity when demand is low and releases it when the grid needs extra supply. The first phase has a storage capacity of 400 MWh, which the Chinese Academy of Sciences says can meet the daily electricity needs of about 200,000 people. Although the project has been described as a liquid metal battery on occasion, it is based on vanadium redox flow battery technology. Energy is stored using liquid electrolytes kept in huge tanks. This technology was created at the Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics (DICP), an institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the installation was done by Rongke Power.How the Dalian battery stores electricityIn contrast to conventional batteries that house their chemicals within the cell, the active chemicals for a flow battery are mostly housed externally in tanks. In the Dalian project, the liquid electrolyte used in the system has vanadium ions. The fluids are pumped into electrochemical cells, where chemical reactions convert electrical energy into chemical energy. When electricity is needed, the process reverses. The chemical reactions generate electricity, which is then distributed to the grid. The capacity of energy storage in such a system is dependent mostly on the amount of electrolyte in the tanks, while power generation depends on the stack of cells. The advantage of the system is that one can scale up capacity by increasing the number of tanks without necessarily scaling up the cell stacks to the same extent.The first phase can store 400 MWh The Dalian Flow Battery Energy Storage Peak-Shaving Power Station came online to the grid in September 2022 and it officially started to generate power on October 30, 2022. The first stage of its development was planned to have a capacity of 100 megawatts with an energy storage of 400 MWh and run for four hours at full load. The project was planned to reach 200 MW and 800 MWh after a second phase. According to the Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics, the first phase's capacity could meet the daily electricity needs of approximately 200,000 residents. This estimate refers to people, not 200,000 homes. It acts as a buffer for the grid, charging up when demand is low or renewable power is plentiful and discharging when demand is high.Long-lasting alternative to conventional batteriesThe vanadium flow batteries have a water-based electrolyte, which makes them less flammable than regular battery materials. The electrolyte used in vanadium flow batteries is reusable and the system is designed to charge and discharge repeatedly. In contrast to batteries that store their active materials inside the cells, flow batteries store their electrolyte in separate tanks. This design allows the batteries to be used for a long time, and their energy storage capacity grows with larger volumes of liquid electrolyte. However, the pumps, cell stacks and other equipment need regular maintenance and can reduce performance.China built large-scale electricity storage because power from renewable sources varies over time. Solar and wind stations don’t generate electricity at a steady rate, while demand shifts through the day. Such storage facilities allow moving electricity from peak production periods to peak consumption periods. The Dalian station shows how large tanks with liquid electrolyte can store energy from renewable sources and stabilise the electricity grid. It is not a liquid metal battery and the 200,000 people number does not mean that the facility serves 200,000 households. It is a large vanadium flow battery designed to stabilise China’s electricity grid.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1992, Spain placed 358 concrete anti-trawling reefs off Alicante to protect 540 hectares of seagrass; eight years later, researchers observed partial meadow recovery
articles.summary: Discover how Spain's innovative 1992 anti-trawling reefs have led to the gradual recovery of seagrass meadows, highlighting the challenges and successes in preserving Posidonia oceanica in the Mediterranean region.
articles.body: Some damage can be done in hours, yet take almost a century to undo. Seagrass meadows show how. Trawling involves dragging a heavy net along the seabed to catch fish. Repeated trawling can uproot 100,000 to 360,000 seagrass shoots every hour, according to a technical report commissioned by the European Commission on Posidonia beds. Illegal trawling off Alicante in southeast Spain had already damaged local seagrass meadows. So, in 1992, Spain placed 358 concrete anti-trawling reefs on the seabed to protect 540 hectares of seagrass. Eight years later, researchers saw partial meadow recovery.A slow-growing meadow under threat The plant from the story is Posidonia oceanica, which is a seagrass that grows only in the Mediterranean Sea. Its leaves grow up to a metre long during the summer season. Its meadow hosts many different kinds of animals and algae. The report's authors, Elena Díaz-Almela and Carlos M. Duarte, refer to the plant as a nursery ground for several commercially important species. However, this plant only grows one to six centimetres in length per year, so losses become very difficult to reverse. Their review of 39 studies at 135 locations found that 46% of the Mediterranean meadows had lost some range, density or cover. Some 20% had regressed significantly since the 1970s.What Spain did off AlicanteDíaz-Almela and Duarte call this one of the first uses of artificial reefs to protect a Posidonia meadow. The work began in 1992 in El Campello and Villajoyosa, in Alicante. Illegal otter trawling, a form of bottom trawling, damaged 40% of the seagrass beds at depths of 14 to 28 metres. In total, it covered 290 hectares along more than seven kilometres of shoreline. The reefs were heavy concrete structures. Any trawling gear that runs over them gets caught and breaks up. The 358 reefs, arranged in rows that were 300 meters long, protected 540 hectares of meadow from trawling. The work was accompanied by a follow-up research programme to see what happened next.Recovery came, but slowly Eight years later, researchers discovered partial recovery of the meadow due to rhizome growth. Rhizomes are underground stems that help the spreading of the plant. However, there is a catch. The Commission report adds that rhizome growth in the meadows impacted by trawling was five times slower than in the healthy meadows at the same depth. There was also four times less light, as the seabed sediment had changed. In 2005, José M. González-Correa and colleagues published ‘Recovery of deep Posidonia oceanica meadows degraded by trawling,’ which investigated a similar area. It was affected by illegal trawling and protected by reefs. The researchers compared two areas that were affected by trawling and two that were left untouched. Growth was positive in both cases but lower in the affected meadows. The authors conclude that recovery is possible if the cause of the damage is eliminated. They say that extremely slow growth can make the process last almost a century. Why reefs are not a magic fixThe report is careful about what the reefs can deliver. The trawlers are often too big for the reefs built so far. They can be two to five times more powerful than officially declared engine ratings suggest. Illegal trawlers can then move the reefs and continue fishing in the meadows. Many reef projects do not have monitoring, and so it is difficult to say how they are doing, the authors note. At Cap Couronne in France, reefs and daily surveillance prevented trawling within the meadow. But some of it went to a nearby unprotected patch. Both the Commission report and the González-Correa team suggest one lesson: the best way to protect a seagrass meadow is probably to avoid losing it in the first place.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2019, German researchers buried water pipes 4 cm beneath a 4 m² road slab; in field tests, the slab stayed above 0°C and remained clear during two roughly 5-cm snowfalls
articles.summary: Discover how German scientists developed heated concrete slabs that stay snow-free in winter, potentially reducing road accidents and reliance on harmful salt treatments.
articles.body: If you have ever slipped on an icy pavement, you probably already know the feeling. Your heart jumps, your coffee spills, and it feels like your entire morning is ruined. A small German experiment hints at a quieter fix for this problem. According to a 2020 study published in SN Applied Sciences, scientists from the University of Erlangen-Nürnberg and the China University of Geosciences studied concrete slabs heated with mild water at temperatures found in groundwater. The outdoor slab remained above freezing even with all the snowfall.Why winter roads need a better fix Winter brings too many dangers on the roads. The authors note that accident rates in Germany are usually high in winter compared to other times of the year. The usual fixes have their own drawbacks. Road salt increases levels of chloride in groundwater, while snowploughs can damage roads. A US Geological Survey study published in Science of the Total Environment reveals that mean chloride levels in streams in the northern US analysed in the research roughly doubled from 1990 to 2011. There were also increases in levels of chloride outside the salting period. This means that chloride accumulates in shallow groundwater in winter and is released gradually throughout the year. While they were American streams, they did show how salt can remain in the water system.How the team tested it Pipes were placed about 4 cm below the surface of concrete slabs. The water in them was mild, not hot. In lab tests, it ran between 8°C and 14°C, the range found in groundwater around Nuremberg. The slabs were kept in a cooling chamber that could go as low as -10°C. With a pipe spacing of 10 cm, water at 10°C kept the surface above the freezing point. The water at 8°C failed when the chamber got down to about -9°C. If the pipes were 20 cm apart, the water needed to be at least 12°C to keep the surface reliably ice-free. For the real-world test, researchers built outdoor slabs of 2 m by 2 m, which is 4 m² each, in a university backyard in Erlangen. The pipes were again about 4 cm deep. The test ran from 15 January to 10 March 2019. The lowest air temperature recorded was -9°C, but the heated surface remained above 0°C throughout the whole period. The comparison slab, unheated, was sometimes below freezing.What happened when it snowedDuring this test, there were two snowfalls, each with a snow depth of about 5 cm. During both of them, the heated surface was free of any snow. For one recorded snow event on 26 January 2019, the surface cooled from roughly 3°C to 1°C. However, it remained above freezing point. In that run, the temperature of the water supply was only 8°C. When it was snowing, the slab was extracting more heat from the water, roughly 60 to 180 watts per square metre. After the snow stopped, the heat demand slowly dropped back to around 60 watts per square metre.Why cities may have an edge and what is still unknown Cities are usually warmer than rural areas, and the ground beneath them warms up, too. The team suspected an urban heat island effect in Nuremberg. There, the paper reports groundwater temperatures of 14°C to 15°C in the city centre. Nearby rural areas were usually above 9°C. They also say the outdoor test maintained the slab snow-free without supplemental heating.Before anyone digs up a road, a little caution is necessary. The slabs were small, and it took about two months for the outdoor test. The authors describe the winter as rather mild and call for long-term studies. Only two snowfalls were recorded during the period. The method also tested Nuremberg’s climate and groundwater. The authors believe that supplementary heating, such as a heat pump, would be required in extreme frost below -10°C. The team planned to keep monitoring the Erlangen test field over the long term. The test was only a promising first look for now, not a complete answer. However, if it works on a bigger scale, it could mean safer roads in winter, but with less salt.You use AI every day. articles.title: Daniel Craig returned to the National Youth Theatre for its 70th-anniversary celebration; the institution has helped launch the careers of Helen Mirren, Chiwetel Ejiofor and Ed Sheeran
articles.summary: Daniel Craig returned to the National Youth Theatre (NYT) for a special celebration marking the organisation's 70th anniversary, joining a gathering of
articles.body: Daniel Craig returned to the National Youth Theatre (NYT) for a special celebration marking the organisation's 70th anniversary, joining a gathering of performers, writers and emerging artists at London's Royal Festival Hall. The event brought together several generations of creative talent to reflect on the opportunities and experiences that shaped their careers. The institution, which has helped launch the careers of some of Britain's best-known performers, including Helen Mirren, Chiwetel Ejiofor and musician Ed Sheeran, used the occasion to celebrate its longstanding contribution to the country's creative industries.Daniel Craig returns to National Youth Theatre for its 70th anniversaryThe anniversary celebration took place on Sunday, September 20, 2026, at the Southbank Centre's Royal Festival Hall in London. Titled ‘Letters to My Younger Future Self,’ the event was organised to mark seven decades of the National Youth Theatre of Great Britain and brought together established performers and members of its current generation.According to the National Youth Theatre, the occasion featured a special appearance by Craig, who is both an alumnus and patron of the organisation. He joined a 70-strong cast of current NYT performers and former members for an evening built around personal reflections and messages addressed to their younger selves.The event was supported by Netflix and brought together actors, writers, comedians and other creative figures. The format allowed participants to look back at their early ambitions, discuss the experiences that influenced them and share advice that might have helped them when they were starting out.Craig's appearance was particularly notable because he was not simply attending as a celebrated actor. His connection with the institution stretches back to his own early years in the performing arts.What did the performers share during the celebrationOne of the evening's central moments involved Craig reading a letter written by playwright James Graham. According to the National Youth Theatre, Craig reflected on the importance of stopping, standing still and allowing things to develop rather than accepting that the future must follow a predetermined path.He dedicated the letter to people who had chosen to pause, remain committed to their work and create opportunities for others. Craig was joined by several other familiar names from the entertainment industry. These included Susan Wokoma, Rose Ayling-Ellis, India Amarteifio, Fehinti Balogun, Jessica Henwick, Jack Thorne, James Graham, Daniel Ings, Calam Lynch, Rob Rinder, Fay Ripley and Rhea Norwood.The performances also included lighter moments. Jack Thorne, the creator and co-writer of Adolescence, used his letter to reflect humorously on ageing and the changes that come with time before offering a more serious message about treating others kindly and trying to improve.Rose Ayling-Ellis shared a personal reflection on growing up Deaf and the challenges of trying to fit into a world that was not designed around her experiences.The institution behind several familiar namesThe National Youth Theatre's influence extends well beyond the actors who appeared at the anniversary event. Its alumni list includes performers who have gone on to establish successful careers across film, television, music and theatre.According to the organisation's official alumni page, former members include Helen Mirren, Daniel Craig, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Ed Sheeran, Rosamund Pike, Daniel Day-Lewis, David Oyelowo, Orlando Bloom, Colin Firth, Vanessa Kirby and Ben Kingsley.The list also highlights the institution's contribution to areas of entertainment that do not always receive the same public attention. Its former members include costume and fashion designers, production managers, lighting designers, technical specialists and creative leaders at major cultural venues.The organisation's partnership with Netflix has also contributed to this work. According to NYT, the partnership, which began in 2023, has helped create more than 4,000 free opportunities aimed at encouraging young people to explore careers behind the scenes in the creative industries.Mobius Industries reported the experience of a 16-year-old participant from Liverpool who particularly valued meeting and making friends with people they might not otherwise have encountered. It also reported about former members from the original youth theatre production of Henry V, now in their 80s, who reunited to film the St Crispin's Day speech.You use AI every day. articles.title: 18-year-old Australian pilot Rose Donald flew solo around the country for 40 days, covering 15,000km and raising about $80,000 to help seriously ill children reach specialist care
articles.summary: Australian teenager Rose Donald has completed a 40-day solo flight around the country, covering about 15,000km while raising money for children who need
articles.body: Australian teenager Rose Donald has completed a 40-day solo flight around the country, covering about 15,000km while raising money for children who need specialist medical care. The Melbourne Year 12 student became the youngest female pilot to fly solo around Australia in a general aviation aircraft, pending verification of her record. She turned 18 during the journey and completed 25 legs, spending about 100 hours in the air. Her fundraising supported Little Wings, a charity that provides free air and ground transport for seriously ill children in regional and remote Australia. ABC’s Behind the News reported that she put the total at about $80,000.How Rose Donald completed a 15,000 km solo flight around Australia in 40 daysDonald began the journey as part of her path towards becoming a professional pilot. She already held a private pilot’s licence, and the trip allowed her to build the solo flying hours needed for future commercial pilot training. According to ABC, she received sponsorship from companies whose logos appeared on her aircraft, helping cover the costs of the journey.Over 40 days, Donald flew around Australia’s coastline in a general aviation aircraft, completing 25 legs and about 100 hours of flying. Some individual flights lasted several hours, including a five-and-a-half-hour leg from Launceston in Tasmania to Mallacoota on Victoria’s far eastern coast. She also had to balance the journey with Year 12 schoolwork.When she returned to Essendon Fields in Melbourne, Donald said the experience had made her more confident both as a pilot and as a young adult. Kids News reported that she had spent more than a month living independently and described the trip as valuable preparation for life after high school.Teen pilot raised thousands for Little Wings medical flights for sick childrenDonald partnered with Little Wings during the flight to raise money and awareness for children living in regional and remote areas. The charity provides free ongoing air and ground transport for seriously ill children travelling to specialist medical treatment in major cities. Donald had raised enough to support 42 regional and remote families with children's specialist treatment.ABC’s Behind the News reported a higher figure of about $80,000 when it interviewed Donald, with the pilot explaining that the fundraising had grown into something much bigger than her original career-building goal. She said the charity's work helped reduce the strain on families by making it easier for seriously ill children to access healthcare.Little Wings CEO Clare Pearson praised Donald's effort and said the young pilot had helped spread awareness of the organisation around Australia. The charity has transported sick children from NSW, Queensland and the ACT to specialist care, with Kids News reporting that it had flown five million kilometres since 2012.Donald is now focused on completing school and continuing towards an aviation career. She said the trip had improved her flying skills and confidence while allowing her to contribute to a cause supporting families who need medical transport.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Oh wow, fantastic': Trump reacts as Philippine prez sends fried chicken as late-night 'taste of Manila'
articles.summary: Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
articles.body: Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr. arranged a late-night delivery of fried chicken from homegrown fast-food chain Jollibee for US president Donald Trump and his delegation during their brief stay in Manila. Describing the gesture as a 'taste of Manila', Marcos said he wanted the American president to sample one of the Philippines’ best-known fast-food brands.Marcos revealed the gesture on Wednesday during his meeting with Trump at the presidential palace, saying he had arranged the delivery the previous night because the US president was pressed for time.“Since you’re strapped for time, I thought a taste of Manila might be good. So last night, I asked my staff to have some Jollibee delivered as a late night snack for you and your delegation,” Marcos said.He described Jollibee as a popular Filipino chain and highlighted its fried chicken as one of its main offerings. Marcos also made a claim about the brand’s popularity in the US, drawing an approving response from Trump.“Jollibee … is a very, very popular chain. And one of their main products is fried chicken. And we are very proud to say that we have surpassed KFC in the United States in terms of popularity,” Marcos said according to news agency AP.“Oh wow. Fantastic,” Trump replied.“So we thought that that will give you a taste of, of, of Manila,” Marcos continued. “And, I think, I hope some of your staff was also able to partake.”“You have been working very hard, Mr. President, so just think of it as providing extra energy for all the work that you have to do that you have done and continue to do, and that is in front of you,” he added.It was not clear whether Trump had actually eaten the food.The gesture also appeared to draw on Trump’s known preference for fast food, particularly McDonald’s.In April, Trump received two bags of McDonald’s delivered to the Oval Office through DoorDash, in an event organised by the White House to promote an administration initiative on taxes on overtime and tips.“I like cleanliness, and I think you’re better off going there than maybe someplace that you have no idea where the food’s coming from. It’s a certain standard,” Trump said in a 2016 interview with CNN.Jollibee, which began as an ice cream business in Manila in the 1970s, has grown into one of the Philippines’ best-known brands. The company operates more than 1,600 outlets across 17 countries, with an expanding presence in the US.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Greenpeace activists dumped around 15 tonnes of boulders into the North Sea, which have unexpectedly overlapped with a planned £12 billion windfarm project off England's coast
articles.summary: Greenpeace activists have placed around 15 tonnes of boulders on the seabed off England’s east coast to prevent industrial fishing vessels from damaging
articles.body: Greenpeace activists have placed around 15 tonnes of boulders on the seabed off England’s east coast to prevent industrial fishing vessels from damaging marine habitats and threatening harbour porpoises. However, the underwater barrier has created an unexpected complication: much of it overlaps with the site of two planned offshore windfarms worth £12 billion, backed by the UK government and Andy Burnham.The boulders were placed as part of a campaign against bottom trawling, a fishing method that involves dragging heavy nets across the seabed. Greenpeace said the intervention was intended to protect a marine conservation area where fishing activity has continued despite its protected status. The organisation has since discovered that its chosen location also overlaps with plans for the Norfolk Vanguard windfarm development, raising questions about how the rocks could affect its construction.The incident has brought two environmental priorities into conflict: protecting marine ecosystems from intensive fishing and expanding renewable energy infrastructure.Why is Greenpeace protesting?The protest centres on the Southern North Sea Marine Protected Area (MPA), a designated conservation zone along England’s east coast. The area is important for harbour porpoises, small marine mammals related to dolphins that rely on sound to navigate, communicate and locate food.The Southern North Sea supports nearly 20% of the UK North Sea harbour porpoise population. Its protected status is intended to reduce disturbances to the animals and maintain the availability of their prey. However, the designation does not prohibit every form of fishing throughout the area, and industrial fishing continues in much of the zone.Greenpeace has raised concerns about bottom trawling, a technique in which fishing vessels drag large, weighted nets along the seabed to catch fish living near the ocean floor. The equipment can disturb seabed habitats, damage marine ecosystems and capture animals that are not the intended target.The practice can also affect harbour porpoises indirectly. Intensive fishing can reduce the availability of fish on which the animals depend, while underwater noise from fishing vessels can interfere with their ability to locate prey using echolocation.According to Greenpeace's analysis, bottom trawlers recorded more than 37,200 hours of fishing activity in the Southern North Sea MPA in 2025, making it the most heavily bottom-trawled offshore protected area in the UK that year.The organisation argued that the continued activity undermined the purpose of the conservation designation. After announcing in June that it would take direct action if stronger protections were not introduced, Greenpeace deployed its vessel, the Arctic Sunrise, to place large boulders on the seabed.Each stone weighed up to 2 tonnes. Dropped at strategic positions, the rocks were intended to obstruct the heavy nets used by bottom trawlers, making it difficult for vessels to drag their equipment through the designated area. Greenpeace said the barrier effectively closed around 116 square kilometres of the MPA to bottom trawling. It named the zone an 'Ocean Park' and planned to patrol the area to discourage other forms of industrial fishing.The action was also intended to draw attention to the gap between an area's official conservation status and the activities that are still permitted within it.What is Andy Burnham's offshore windfarm plan?The boulder operation took place just days before the announcement of a major offshore wind investment off the coast of Norfolk. The project, known as Norfolk Vanguard, is being developed by German energy company RWE in partnership with US private equity firm KKR.The £12 billion investment package will fund two offshore windfarms, Vanguard East and Vanguard West. The projects are expected to generate approximately 2.8 gigawatts of electricity, enough to supply around three million homes. The UK government is also contributing £1 billion through its state-owned National Wealth Fund. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027, with the windfarms scheduled to start supplying electricity by 2030.Andy Burnham has backed the investment, describing it as an important development for Britain's energy sector. The project is also expected to support around 2,300 jobs each year through its construction supply chain, alongside approximately 100 permanent jobs once the windfarms are operational.Offshore wind is an important part of the UK's plans to expand renewable electricity generation, reduce dependence on fossil fuels and strengthen domestic energy supplies. The Norfolk Vanguard development is among the country's largest planned offshore wind projects.How did the boulders interfere with the project?The complication emerged when it became clear that most of the boulders Greenpeace had placed on the seabed overlapped with the area earmarked for Norfolk Vanguard East.The organisation had reportedly checked the seabed for existing cables, pipelines and shipwrecks before deploying the rocks. However, it was unaware of the planned windfarm development when it selected the locations. The boulders were placed without permission from the Marine Management Organisation (MMO), the government body responsible for regulating activities in English waters.The rocks could complicate the developers' preparations because offshore windfarm construction requires detailed surveys of the seabed. Developers need to understand the location of obstacles and assess the ground before installing turbine foundations and laying underwater cables. Unmapped boulders can therefore affect construction planning and may need to be relocated.RWE has begun discussions with Greenpeace to establish the precise locations of the rocks. The company is reviewing its existing seabed surveys and assessing whether the boulders could affect construction or the installation of undersea cables.The rocks are expected to be removed before construction progresses, potentially within the coming months. articles.title: Three women stranded by a nationwide US flight shutdown bought a $48,000 Ford Bronco in North Carolina and drove 27 hours to North Dakota after failing to find a rental car, train or bus home
articles.summary: When a nationwide flight shutdown left three women stranded at an airport in North Carolina, they spent more than an hour trying to find another way home.
articles.body: When a nationwide flight shutdown left three women stranded at an airport in North Carolina, they spent more than an hour trying to find another way home. Rental cars were unavailable, buses were sold out and trains were not an option. Their eventual solution was unusual: they bought a brand-new Ford Bronco for $48,000 and drove nearly 1,500 miles to North Dakota.The group included Tara Harding, a nurse practitioner and clinic owner from Bismarck, North Dakota, and two of her employees, Maressia Cowger and Alisha Maier. They had travelled to Charlotte, North Carolina, for a work-related training programme and were preparing to fly home when the disruption began on November 13.According to a report by CBS News, their flights were rescheduled four times before being cancelled. The three women eventually decided that waiting for another flight was no longer practical.Harding told CBS that her decision was not just about getting herself home. Her two employees had children waiting for them, and the clinic had patients scheduled for Monday morning.No rental cars, buses or trains availableAccording to CBS News, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) had ordered a nationwide ground stop on November 13 after problems involving radar data and communications disrupted air traffic across the United States. The order halted flights for more than four hours and left thousands of travellers dealing with cancellations and delays.The women initially tried to rearrange their journey through Delta Air Lines. But after repeated changes to their flight bookings, they began looking at road and rail options. Harding said they searched for rental cars but found none available within a four-hour radius of Charlotte. Greyhound buses were sold out, and they could not find a suitable Amtrak train or an Uber ride for the long journey to North Dakota.After more than an hour of trying to arrange transport, Harding called her husband. He passed on an idea suggested by his mother: why not buy a car and drive home? The women contacted a nearby Ford dealership. A salesperson agreed to keep the dealership open while they made their way there from Charlotte Douglas International Airport in an Uber.They bought a $48,000 Ford Bronco in less than two hoursThe group reached the dealership at around 7.45 pm. Less than two hours later, they drove away in a new Ford Bronco priced at $48,000. Harding described the purchase as an unexpected decision that happened very quickly. In an interview with NBC News, she recalled being on a three-way call with her husband, the car dealer and her employees as the group tried to work out whether they were really going ahead with the purchase.The choice of vehicle was also made under time pressure. Harding and her husband discussed buying something that would have a good resale value, since she initially considered selling it after reaching North Dakota. Her husband suggested choosing a vehicle they would enjoy driving if they decided to keep it. Harding, who describes herself as a Ford enthusiast, settled on the Bronco.A 27-hour drive across nearly 1,500 milesOnce the paperwork was complete, the three women began their journey from Charlotte to Bismarck. The drive covered approximately 1,500 miles and took 27 hours. They took turns driving and sleeping, stopping mainly at petrol stations and drive-through restaurants for fuel and food. The journey continued through the night, with the women sharing driving responsibilities so they could keep moving towards home.Harding told CBS News that she wanted to get her employees back to their families and be ready for patients at her clinic on Monday. The trip also gave the three colleagues an unexpected opportunity to spend time together outside work. Harding said they bonded during the long drive and had no regrets about the purchase.The family has decided to keep the BroncoHarding had initially considered selling the vehicle once they reached Bismarck. But after the journey, she said she felt attached to it because of the circumstances in which they had bought it. Speaking to CBS News, she said she was now inclined to keep the SUV. Her husband also drove it several times after she returned home and wanted to retain it.The FAA disruption affected thousands of travellers. Around 18,000 flight cancellations had been recorded by Monday, according to media reports. The nationwide ground stop was the longest since the September 11, 2001, attacks.You use AI every day. Party workers tore pages from the book on camera, during which Shaina allegedly tore a photograph of Bal Thackeray.Shiv Sena (UBT) seized on the incident to question the rival faction's claim to Bal Thackeray's legacy.In a post on social media, Sena (UBT) leader Swati Borkar said, "Shame on you Shaina NC. Because all these people are mercenaries, it’s a good thing these black-faced people with white feet have run away!" Raut said."These people have neither any ideology nor any morals, neither a single leader nor any loyalty. All these people who insult the honorable Balasaheb should be publicly flogged! Deliberately twisting an incident to create a false narrative will not be tolerated. Anyone spreading defamatory claims against me will face legal action," she wrote on X."And yes, as I have said, I will tear Mani Shankar Aiyar’s photograph a thousand times over and this is what Balasaheb taught us," she added.Earlier in the day, Shinde-led Sena workers tore pages from Sonia Gandhi's book during a protest in Mumbai, demanding that publisher HarperCollins remove passages on pages 201 and 443.Addressing a press conference, Shaina accused Gandhi of insulting Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar by describing him as a "Hindutva exclusionary"."Sonia Gandhi humiliates Savarkar. articles.title: A Seattle metal detectorist found a Rhode Island man’s class ring on a Puget Sound beach 47 years after his brother lost it to the tide, then flew about 3,000 miles to hand it back in person
articles.summary: A class ring that disappeared from a Washington beach nearly five decades ago has finally found its way home, thanks to a Seattle-based metal detector
articles.body: A class ring that disappeared from a Washington beach nearly five decades ago has finally found its way home, thanks to a Seattle-based metal detector enthusiast who went beyond simply locating its owner. Lucas Thrun travelled nearly 3,000 miles to Rhode Island to personally return the keepsake to Paul Benson, its original owner. The story was first reported by WJAR and was also covered by PEOPLE, which shared additional details about the discovery and the family reunion. Benson, a graduate of St. Raphael Academy in Pawtucket, Rhode Island, had lost the ring in 1979, when his brother Eric borrowed it during a trip to the West Coast. While spending time with friends on a beach near Puget Sound in Washington, Eric took the ring off and placed it on a rock. As the tide came in, the ring was swept away.What followed was a disappearance that lasted 47 years. Eric never told his brother about losing the ring, leaving the incident buried in the past for decades. The missing keepsake resurfaced in November 2025, when Thrun discovered it while searching a Seattle-area beach with a metal detector. According to reports, unusually exposed sections of the shoreline helped make the recovery possible. The ring carried two important clues: the name of St. Raphael Academy and the initials PEB, which helped establish its connection to its original owner.Rather than treating the discovery as another interesting find, Thrun set about tracing the ring’s history. He contacted the school, whose alumni network helped identify Benson as the likely owner. The engraved details and school records eventually helped connect the two.The search for Benson led Thrun and members of the school community to his home in Pawtucket. Benson was initially taken aback by the unexpected visit, having little reason to believe that something lost so long ago could turn up again.Thrun, however, wanted to make the reunion more personal. Instead of sending the ring through the post, he travelled from Seattle to Rhode Island to return it himself. The occasion also brought the two brothers together. Eric, who now lives in Israel, made arrangements to attend the handover, turning the return of a lost piece of jewellery into a family reunion after nearly half a century.For Benson, the ring carried significance beyond its material value. It was a reminder of his school years and brought back memories of his mother, making its return particularly meaningful. The unexpected recovery also restored a connection to a period of his life that he had thought was permanently lost. The story has since taken on another dimension through the involvement of St. Raphael Academy. According to PEOPLE, the school recognised Thrun’s efforts by making him an honorary member of its community, acknowledging the role he played in bringing the ring back to its owner.What began as a summer trip, a borrowed ring and an unfortunate encounter with the tide eventually became a story of patience, community and an extraordinary act of kindness. Nearly 47 years after it disappeared beneath the waters of Puget Sound, the class ring is back where it belongs.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A North Carolina father spent more than $70,000 on a 60,000-light Christmas display that drew families to his street; his HOA objected, and he is now suing as neighbours face a vote on new rules
articles.summary: A North Carolina father who spent more than $70,000 on a 60,000 light Christmas display is now suing his homeowners association after the show turned his
articles.body: A North Carolina father who spent more than $70,000 on a 60,000 light Christmas display is now suing his homeowners association after the show turned his street into a local attraction. Neil Heuer’s annual “High Flying Lights” display in Waxhaw’s Aero Plantation community has drawn families, traffic complaints, an HOA hearing, and proposed rules that could restrict similar displays in the future, according to AOL and Realtor.com.The dispute began as a disagreement over visitor traffic but has grown into a broader fight over property rights, neighbourhood privacy, and how much holiday cheer is too much. Heuer plans to put on another show this year, while residents face a vote on new rules that could shape the community long after the holiday season ends.Why the display drew attentionHeuer’s display includes more than 60,000 synchronized LED lights, lasers, choreographed animatronics, and coordinated music programming. He has been running the show for five years and estimates he has spent more than $70,000 building it.The display has become a local attraction, with families driving through the neighbourhood to see it. Heuer says, as per the reports, that the visitors are mostly families with children in the backseat, and that the show brings him joy because he loves sharing it with people.But the traffic has also created problems. Aero Plantation is a private residential community with an airstrip, tennis courts, and an equestrian centre, and some residents say the influx of cars has made the narrow private roads feel unsafe.What the HOA objected toIn August, the HOA’s legal counsel sent Heuer a letter saying that inviting unknown members of the public into the subdivision was a nuisance. The association argued that the traffic generated by the display violated the community’s declaration.In September, the HOA held a hearing on the display. It found violations related to exterior lighting and signage size but said it could not determine whether parking or architectural changes violated the rules.The HOA warned that future lighting violations could result in fines of $100 per day. It also offered to review proposed changes if Heuer addressed its concerns.The compromise that failedHeuer’s attorney, Shira Hedgepeth, responded with a compromise. She offered to run the display at 30 percent of its maximum brightness, eliminate powerful moving head lights that could project beams into the sky, and remove a yard sign and large banner advertising the show, the reports suggested.The concessions addressed some of the HOA’s lighting concerns but did not fully resolve the traffic issue. On September 28, Heuer allegedly tested a powerful light fixture intended for his Halloween display, and the next day the HOA imposed a $100 fine.Three days later, the HOA’s attorney informed Heuer’s attorney that the board had rejected the compromise. That prompted Heuer to sue the Aero Plantation Association on October 6 in Union County Superior Court.What the lawsuit arguesThe lawsuit challenges the HOA’s interpretation of its own rules. The covenants forbid exterior lighting directed outside the boundaries of a homeowner’s lot, but Heuer’s attorney argues that the HOA is treating lights visible from the street as though they were directed beyond his property.Hedgepeth argues that under that reading, almost any porch light in the neighbourhood would violate the rule. She says the HOA is applying the restriction too broadly.The lawsuit also challenges the association’s enforcement procedures. Heuer says the governing documents require 20 days to correct certain violations before enforcement action, while the HOA threatened daily fines after only six days.New rules could change everythingAfter Heuer filed his lawsuit, the HOA adopted new parking and road use rules. It also circulated proposed amendments that would go further, restricting public attractions and certain types of exterior lighting throughout the neighbourhood.The first amendment would prohibit homeowners from advertising their properties as public attractions or engaging in activities that generate substantial or recurring traffic from nonresidents. It would also restrict activities that cause visitors to stop, park, or line up on neighbourhood streets.The second amendment would prohibit flashing, strobing, pulsing, or repeatedly changing exterior lights visible from neighbouring properties, streets, or common areas. It would also ban certain high intensity beams and give the board authority to set brightness limits and permitted periods for holiday decorations.Why the vote mattersResidents have until January 30 to vote on the proposed amendments. Each amendment requires written approval from at least two thirds of all association lots, not just two thirds of returned ballots.Heuer believes the rules are directed at him. He has urged neighbours to vote against the amendments, arguing that restrictions meant to address his Christmas display could affect the entire neighbourhood long after his family moves away.The HOA president, David Arno, declined to discuss the dispute in detail. He said the association will respond through the appropriate legal process and encouraged homeowners to participate in the vote.What happens nextHeuer plans to go big again this year. He says the proposed rules will not apply to this year’s display, and he intends to put on another show despite the risk of additional fines.The lawsuit is still ongoing. The outcome could determine whether the HOA’s existing restrictions are being applied fairly and whether the proposed amendments are valid.For Heuer, the dispute has taken a personal toll. He and his wife plan to move out of Aero Plantation after their youngest daughter graduates from high school in June 2029, and he says his next neighbourhood will not have an HOA.You use AI every day.
