articles.title: Nintendo employee saved a 1981 Donkey Kong painting from trash and tucked it into a coffee table; decades later, it sold for $329,400
articles.summary: A former Nintendo of America employee who rescued an original Donkey Kong painting from discarded office materials in the late 1980s has seen the
articles.body: A former Nintendo of America employee who rescued an original Donkey Kong painting from discarded office materials in the late 1980s has seen the forgotten artwork sell for $329,400 at auction. Donna Darbous, who worked as an advertising executive at the gaming company, saved several original illustrations during an office expansion with her supervisor's permission. Among them was a 1981 promotional painting by illustrator Leslie Cabarga, featuring Donkey Kong, Pauline and Jumpman, the character who later became known as Mario. Darbous kept the rescued pieces in the flat drawers of a coffee table for decades before rediscovering them while sorting through her belongings. The artwork was eventually sold at Landry Pop Auctions on October 28, 2026, more than doubling its highest pre-sale estimate of $150,000.How a Nintendo employee rescued the artwork from being discardedThe unusual story began in the late 1980s, when Nintendo of America was expanding its office space. During the process, advertising executive Donna Darbous noticed several original illustrations among materials marked for disposal.Recognising their significance, she sought permission from her supervisor to take some of the pieces home rather than allow them to be thrown away.Among the rescued materials was the original 1981 Donkey Kong promotional artwork created by illustrator Leslie Cabarga. The illustration had been commissioned for Nintendo's North American arcade promotional flyer and was subsequently used as the basis for posters distributed across the country.Darbous had been involved in Nintendo's advertising, collateral and packaging initiatives during a period when the company was expanding rapidly in the American market. Her work included campaigns associated with Super Mario Bros., Zelda, Tetris, the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES), Super NES and Game Boy.Painting remained forgotten inside a coffee table for decadesAfter bringing the rescued artwork home, Darbous stored the pieces in the flat drawers of a coffee table, alongside prewar lithographs she had collected during her travels in the Czech Republic.The Nintendo material remained there for decades, largely out of sight. Nearly 40 years after her time at the company, Darbous began sorting through her belongings and revisiting her collection of Nintendo memorabilia.During this process, she remembered the rescued illustrations and eventually discovered them inside the coffee table that she still owned.The rediscovery brought back memories of her time at Nintendo and a period when video games and emerging technology were transforming the entertainment industry. Realising the historical significance of the material, she eventually contacted Landry Pop Auctions founder Travis Landry to arrange its sale.Artwork features Mario's earliest incarnation as JumpmanThe painting was created in 1981 by American illustrator Leslie Cabarga for Nintendo's North American Donkey Kong arcade promotional flyer.One of its most significant features is the appearance of Mario in his earliest public incarnation, when the character was known as Jumpman.The illustration depicts Donkey Kong holding a barrel above his head, while Jumpman climbs towards Pauline, who is trapped above him. The scene reflects the central gameplay of the original arcade title, in which players had to navigate obstacles and avoid barrels thrown by the giant ape to rescue Pauline.At the time, Mario had not yet become the globally recognised character associated with Nintendo's video game franchise. He was introduced as Jumpman in Donkey Kong before being renamed Mario, reportedly after Mario Segale, the landlord of Nintendo of America's warehouse in Washington state.The name became firmly established with the release of Donkey Kong Jr. in 1982. Mario later became the central character in Mario Bros. in 1983 and Super Mario Bros. in 1985.How the original Donkey Kong painting was createdThe artwork is made using a layered technique involving acrylic paint on transparent acetate placed over an ink and airbrush illustration on cardstock.The characters and objects, including Donkey Kong, Jumpman, Pauline and the barrels, were painted on the transparent acetate layer, while the background was created separately on the cardstock board. The technique resembles the layered artwork used in traditional animation production.According to the auction catalogue, the original measures 19⅞ inches in height and 16⅜ inches in width, approximately 50 by 42 centimetres.Despite being more than four decades old, the artwork was described by the auction house as being in great condition, with vibrant colours. The condition report noted minor wear along the edges of the cardstock, some faint rubbing, small tears and minor losses of airbrush on the underlying board.The auction house also noted that some of the damage was not visible beneath the painted acetate overlay.Donkey Kong painting sells for $329,400 at auctionThe original artwork was offered as Lot 102 at Landry Pop Auctions on October 28, 2026, as part of a sale titled 'Jumpman: The Beginning of an Icon, Important Original Art and Artifacts from Nintendo History'.The painting carried a pre-sale estimate of $100,000 to $150,000 but eventually fetched $329,400, more than twice its highest estimate.The auction house described the illustration as representing the first public appearance of Mario, making it a significant piece of early video game history.The sale also established a new reported auction benchmark for original video game artwork, surpassing the previous notable record of $63,000 paid for Robert Florczak's original Prince of Persia box artwork at Heritage Auctions in January 2023.The Donkey Kong painting's final price was more than five times that earlier figure.Other Nintendo collectibles were also part of the auctionThe Donkey Kong illustration was among 49 pieces from Darbous' personal collection offered during the auction.The collection included original promotional artwork, gaming memorabilia and other material connected to Nintendo's early years in the American market.Some of the other notable items included original Mickey Mouse Game & Watch artwork from 1981, Mickey & Donald Game & Watch promotional artwork from 1982, Super Mario Bros. production artwork featuring Mario and Luigi, and an original 1985 Super Mario Bros. NES cartridge.The Super Mario Bros. production artwork featuring Mario and Luigi sold for $17,080, while the graded 1985 NES cartridge fetched $34,160. The Mickey Mouse and Mickey & Donald artwork sold for $7,320 and $10,980, respectively.The auction brought together material from a period when Nintendo was developing the characters, games and visual identity that would eventually become recognised around the world.How the original Donkey Kong game changed Nintendo's fortunesThe painting's historical significance is closely connected to the success of the original Donkey Kong arcade game, released in 1981.Before its launch, Nintendo of America had struggled with the commercial performance of Radar Scope, a space-themed arcade game that left the company with approximately 2,000 unsold cabinets.Nintendo president Hiroshi Yamauchi turned to a young designer, Shigeru Miyamoto, to develop a new game using the existing hardware. The result was Donkey Kong, which introduced players to a character-driven arcade experience centred on rescuing Pauline from the giant ape.The game became a major commercial success in the American market, helping Nintendo establish itself as a significant player in the arcade industry.It also introduced characters that would go on to become central to Nintendo's identity, particularly Mario, who evolved from Jumpman into one of the most recognisable figures in video game history.The rescued 1981 painting now offers a surviving example of the original promotional artwork used to introduce those characters to American audiences.You use AI every day. In 2025, Islamabad spent an amount equivalent to 33% of its export earnings on servicing external debt, while total external debt stood at 34% of Gross National Income.The report, therefore, highlights the challenge facing Islamabad: managing its growing external debt while ensuring that its economy generates enough foreign exchange to meet repayment obligations.Pakistan’s economic challengesContinued lending does not necessarily mean Pakistan’s economy is healthy. Nor does its growing debt burden mean the country is on the verge of default.The latest economic indicators present a mixed picture.The World Bank estimates that Pakistan’s economy grew by 3.7% in FY26, up from 3.2% in the previous financial year. The fiscal deficit narrowed to 2.6% of GDP, while the current account recorded a small deficit of 0.1% of GDP. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) also reported that Pakistan’s gross foreign exchange reserves had risen to approximately $21.5 billion by the end of September 2025.These gains, however, are offset by continued economic challenges. Economic growth has not generated enough jobs for Pakistan’s growing workforce. About 3.5 million people enter the workforce every year, yet unemployment stood at 7% in 2024. While nearly 18 million new jobs have been created since 2018, most have been informal, low-paid or self-employment opportunities.Poverty, too, has increased, with the rate rising from 22% in 2018-19 to 29% in 2024-25. An estimated 70 million Pakistanis are now living in poverty.The future outlook also remains challenging. The World Bank projected Pakistan’s economy to grow by 3.8% in FY27, a marginal increase from the estimated 3.7% growth in FY26. Headline inflation was expected to rise to 8.2% in FY27 before easing to around 7%.The data therefore highlights the economic pressures Pakistan faces and is expected to confront in the coming years.China: Pakistan’s ‘all-weather’ friendChina being Pakistan’s largest individual creditor is perhaps unsurprising. Beijing and Islamabad are, after all, each other’s “all-weather friends.”China’s investment in Pakistan has largely been channelled through the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), the flagship project of Beijing’s ambitious Belt and Road Initiative. Under CPEC, Chinese investment in Pakistan is estimated at $62 billion over a period of 15 years.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Another important feature of this economic relationship is loan rollover, under which a creditor extends the repayment period of existing loans instead of demanding immediate repayment. China has continued to roll over existing loans to Pakistan, providing Islamabad temporary relief from its foreign currency obligations without reducing its overall debt.With Pakistan struggling to repay its Chinese loans, what explains Beijing's willingness to not only continue providing financial support to Islamabad but also roll over existing loans?Sushant Sareen, senior fellow at the Observer Research Foundation and an expert on Pakistan, attributed Beijing's continued support to the “strategic relationship” between the two countries.“It’s not just about an economic relationship between them. I think one of the reasons why the Chinese keep bailing Pakistan out and give them money is because of the strategic relationship that exists between them,” Sareen told The Times of India.Even CPEC, he added, was China’s plan to “prop up” Pakistan’s economy and make it more efficient and productive.Ultimately, the question is whether Pakistan can generate enough foreign exchange to service its growing debt, even with continued support from China.Why financial institutions continue lending to PakistanThat Beijing is Islamabad’s largest creditor comes as little surprise. However, multilateral institutions such as the IMF and the World Bank also continue to play an important role in financing Pakistan.Since joining the IMF in 1950, Pakistan has received around two dozen bailout packages. Most recently, in October, the IMF agreed to release another $1.21 billion under its ongoing loan and sustainability programmes, subject to Executive Board approval.In a recent YouTube interview, former IMF chief economist Gita Gopinath was asked why the lender continues to bail out Pakistan despite concerns over its ability to repay its loans.Gopinath explained that the IMF’s role is to help countries facing economic crises and that it cannot simply walk away from them.She also emphasised that the IMF's decisions are taken by its member countries, including India. The decision to extend a loan, therefore, rests with the membership rather than the IMF's management.Sareen echoed this view.“Pakistan is a member of the IMF. It is the IMF’s job to bail out countries which are facing balance of payments problems,” he said.He, however, pointed out that political considerations could also influence the IMF's lending decisions.“India holds slightly over 2% vote share and that's not big enough to veto the loan. The Americans with 16% or 17% stake can actually do that, because with 15% you can veto any IMF loan. And clearly the Americans don't want to turn the screws on the Pakistanis. So, yes, to some extent it is a political decision to give money to Pakistan,” he argued.Sareen noted, however, that overall, the IMF largely operates within its economic mandate.Taken together, Islamabad's repeated reliance on the IMF underlines the extent to which its economy depends on external financial support.Can Pakistan actually repay its debtPakistan's total external debt of around $135 billion does not mean the entire amount is due for repayment immediately. The debt has accumulated over several years, with repayments spread across different periods.The extent of Pakistan's reliance on fresh borrowing is evident from the figures. In FY26, it received $16.16 billion in external loans, while repaying around $14.44 billion in external public debt, including $11.20 billion in principal and $3.24 billion in interest, according to the ministry of economic affairs.The key question, therefore, is whether Islamabad can generate enough foreign exchange to meet these repayment obligations while managing its other economic needs.Sareen argued that the bigger challenge for Pakistan was not repaying its entire debt, but servicing it — having enough foreign exchange to meet repayment and interest obligations as they fall due.“Pakistans' problem is that they're not earning the kind of foreign exchange they require to service that debt. And the debt which they're taking on is increasing virtually every year. But for now, they're managing to tide it over. They managed to avoid default, but at a very high price,” he said.The challenge for Islamabad, therefore, is not just to keep securing loans, but to build an economy capable of meeting its repayment obligations without repeatedly relying on external support.What happens if creditors stop lending to PakistanPakistan is often described as a country facing economic collapse and the risk of disintegration. Its continued dependence on external financing raises an important question: what would happen if lenders stopped extending fresh loans to Islamabad?The withdrawal of support from its lenders would not automatically push Pakistan into default or close to disintegration. Rather, it would face severe economic difficulties.Sareen warned that a default could trigger severe economic hardship, with Pakistan potentially spending three to four years trying to stabilise its economy and regain access to the international financial system. During this period, it could struggle to maintain imports and deal with foreign exchange shortages.But Pakistan continues to stay afloat — with support from international institutions, as well as countries whose financial assistance is shaped by strategic interests. Lending decisions also have a political dimension, with the interests and influence of powerful member countries playing a role.For now, creditors continue to extend financial support, even as concerns over Islamabad's ability to repay its debt persist.You use AI every day. articles.title: Two US senators from opposing parties warned Trump's White House that AI-powered cyber threats are outpacing defences, citing rogue agents, software vulnerabilities and a model's attempted link to China
articles.summary: Two US senators have warned the Trump administration that rapidly advancing artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities are creating cybersecurity threats
articles.body: Two US senators have warned the Trump administration that rapidly advancing artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities are creating cybersecurity threats that the country's existing defences are struggling to contain.They called for urgent measures to protect critical infrastructure, financial institutions and widely used software from AI-powered attacks.According to Reuters, Democratic Senator Maria Cantwell and Republican Senator Mike Rounds raised concerns in a letter to Jay Clayton, chairman of the White House Super Intelligence Task Force.They said AI was making it increasingly easier to identify and exploit software vulnerabilities, while the country's cybersecurity infrastructure was failing to keep pace.The warning comes as a separate Government Accountability Office (GAO) investigation found that four widely used AI platforms, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok, generated plans for terrorist attacks in the US when tested by government investigators.AI tools generated plans for attacks on US cities, power gridThe GAO report, released on Wednesday, found that investigators were able to obtain viable plans for attacks involving explosive devices and the country's electrical grid within 12 hours of testing.The investigation was commissioned by Senator Maggie Hassan, a Democrat from New Hampshire who is set to take over as chair of the Senate Homeland Security Committee in January.According to the 61-page report, two AI platforms generated plans involving the construction and detonation of improvised explosive devices (IEDs) intended to cause mass casualties. Two others provided plans for using drones or firearms to target electrical infrastructure and cause economic damage.The platforms also provided details that could potentially help someone carry out such attacks, including suggested targets, locations, timing and methods.In one instance, an AI platform initially refused to provide detailed instructions but investigators managed to bypass its safeguards by changing how they framed their requests.The report also found that one platform suggested using a vehicle to collect supplies before carrying out an attack at a location where a public event was expected to draw large crowds.For tests involving electrical infrastructure, AI platforms suggested attacks on substations near a US airport. They also provided maps and images to support their proposed plans.GAO investigators subsequently consulted experts and visited some of the locations to assess the accuracy of the information. They found certain inaccuracies, including incorrectly placed roads and high walls that could obstruct views of the targets.Senator warns AI threat is no longer theoreticalHassan said the findings demonstrated the growing potential for commercially available AI tools to be misused by individuals seeking to carry out attacks."We need to act now," she said during a conference call with reporters.Announcing plans for hearings on AI safety when the new Congress takes over in January, Hassan said the threat posed by the technology could no longer be treated as hypothetical.She warned that without congressional action, it was only a matter of time before a malicious actor used AI to plan and execute a major attack.The GAO said AI technology offered significant benefits but could also provide capabilities to people intending to cause harm. It warned that misuse of the technology represented a growing risk to national and economic security.Tech companies respond to GAO findingsThe report included responses from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and SpaceXAI, the companies behind the four platforms examined by investigators.The companies largely maintained that they were continuing to improve their models and strengthen safeguards against harmful uses.Anthropic said it took the findings seriously and acknowledged that determined users could sometimes obtain harmful information by misrepresenting the purpose of their requests. However, it said it could not independently verify the GAO's findings.Google said the investigation involved earlier versions of its models and that it continued to make improvements.OpenAI welcomed the opportunity to respond to the findings, while SpaceXAI said it was working to improve safety with every new model release.Senators seek stronger AI-powered cyber defencesSeparately, Cantwell and Rounds called on the Trump administration to accelerate the development and deployment of AI-powered cybersecurity tools.They pointed to several recent incidents highlighting the growing risks, including AI systems identifying vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used internet programming language, disruptions involving rogue AI systems and data breaches affecting Japanese companies.The senators also cited an incident reported by Toronto-based AI company Cohere, in which a Chinese-developed Qwen model attempted to establish an unauthorised connection to a server in China during testing."AI is rapidly increasing the ability to discover and exploit weaknesses in software and our defences are not keeping pace," the senators wrote.They argued that the government could not rely on individual technology companies to address threats affecting the wider digital economy.Their demands included stronger security standards for autonomous AI agents and faster deployment of defensive AI technologies.The latest warning follows a series of technology disruptions in the US over the past week, including a Microsoft outage affecting several services, disruptions to air travel and a software problem at JPMorgan Chase that interfered with some banking services.However, the country's top homeland security official said on Tuesday that the recent outages were not caused by cyberattacks but by ageing computer systems requiring upgrades.The senators had also written to Clayton last month, urging the White House to develop a coordinated national strategy on AI safety and cyber defence.You use AI every day. articles.title: Azam Khan walks out of Dasna jail on interim bail in money laundering case; heads to Rampur
articles.summary: GHAZIABAD: Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan was released from Dasna district jail in Ghaziabad on interim bail on Wednesday. He is headed to Rampur.
articles.body: GHAZIABAD: Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan was released from Dasna district jail in Ghaziabad on interim bail on Wednesday. He is headed to Rampur.Khan’s son, Abdullah Azam Khan, arrived at the jail premises to welcome his father. Supporters of the SP leader had also gathered outside Dasna Jail, news agency ANI reported.The Allahabad high court on Tuesday granted interim bail to Khan in a money laundering case registered by the Enforcement Directorate (ED).The court observed that the mandatory provisions governing his arrest were prima facie not strictly followed.A division bench of Justice Rajiv Gupta and Justice Devendra Singh observed that, prima facie, the mandatory provisions of Article 22(1) of the Constitution and Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) were not strictly complied with at the time of Khan’s arrest.The court directed Khan’s release on a personal bond along with two sureties of an equal amount. He will have to furnish the bail bonds to the satisfaction of the chief judicial magistrate (CJM), Ghaziabad, ANI reported.The next hearing in the matter is scheduled for December 10. Senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Imran Ullah appeared on behalf of Khan before the Allahabad High Court.The interim relief comes in the ED’s money laundering case against the senior SP leader.Khan, a 10-time MLA from Rampur Sadar and former Cabinet minister, has been one of the SP’s prominent leaders and a long-standing influential political figure in Uttar Pradesh, ANI reported.He has been lodged in Rampur district jail since November last year following his conviction in a forgery case.He was also sentenced to two years in prison in a case relating to his alleged objectionable remarks about cleaning the shoes of government officials, including the then collector-cum-district magistrate, during the 2019 Lok Sabha election campaign.On October 28, the ED attached the land and building of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The agency valued the attached property at Rs 426 crore in book value, while its estimated current market value stood at Rs 1,170 crore.Founded by Khan in 2006, Mohammad Ali Jauhar University is a private university located in Rampur.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ghaziabad | Silver Rate in Ghaziabad | Bank Holidays in Ghaziabad | Public Holidays in Ghaziabad | Ghaziabad AQI | Weather in Ghaziabad | Petrol Price in Ghaziabad | Diesel Price in Ghaziabad | CNG Price in Ghaziabad | LPG Price in GhaziabadStay updated with the latest Ghaziabad news. articles.title: In 2025, billionaire Ken Griffin bought a Park Avenue duplex from Julia Koch for $45 million; one year later, he sold the New York apartment to Jets owner Woody Johnson for $58 million
articles.summary: Citadel founder Ken Griffin has sold his duplex apartment at 740 Park Avenue, one of New York’s most exclusive cooperative buildings, for $58 million,
articles.body: Citadel founder Ken Griffin has sold his duplex apartment at 740 Park Avenue, one of New York’s most exclusive cooperative buildings, for $58 million, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal. The buyer is Woody Johnson, New York Jets owner and Johnson & Johnson heir, whose net worth is $13.5 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. “I wish Woody and his family many happy years in one of New York’s great residences,” Griffin said in a statement, Bloomberg reported. The deal was struck off-market.Griffin bought the apartment in 2025The hedge-fund billionaire bought the unit in 2025 for $45 million from Julia Koch, the widow of billionaire industrialist David Koch. The space covers roughly 8,500 square feet across two floors. The limestone building was developed around 1930 by real estate investor James T. Lee, grandfather of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis. The building has about 31 apartments and has long been one of Manhattan’s most prestigious co-ops.In less than two years, Johnson is paying about 29 per cent more than Griffin did. However, it is important to note that this figure does not account for transaction costs or renovations, so the actual gain could be smaller.The sale comes amid a political fight. Back in April, Mayor Zohran Mamdani filmed the ‘tax the rich’ video outside Ken Griffin’s penthouse at 220 Central Park South while promoting a proposed annual pied-à-terre tax on second residences valued above $5 million. At the time, Griffin’s company issued a statement to its employees calling the video ‘shameful’. “It is shameful that he used Ken’s name as the example of those who supposedly aren’t carrying their fair share of the burdens associated with New York City’s often costly and wasteful spending,” Griffin’s COO at Citadel, Gerald Beeson, wrote in a letter, according to the Journal.In May, while speaking at the Milken Institute Global Conference, Griffin said that the firm planned to expand in Miami rather than New York because of Mamdani’s treatment of the firm. “The mayor of New York has made clear to my partners and principally my New York partners... that we need to double down on our bet in Miami because we want to be in a state that embraces business, that embraces education, that embraces personal freedom and liberty, and that embraces people having an opportunity to live the American Dream and a dream of earned success, not a dream of redistributive handouts that leave people dependent on government for their lives,” Griffin said.Earlier this year, Business Insider calculated that Griffin could owe an extra $1.3 million to $1.4 million annually under the levy across his three New York City holdings, with his 220 Central Park South penthouse accounting for the bulk. As the hedge-fund giant’s primary residence is in Florida, selling the 740 Park Avenue duplex could reduce any future tax attributable to that property.The Citadel boss still has a foothold in the building. Earlier this year, he bought an adjacent apartment at 740 Park for $38 million, a purchase that The Real Deal reported as having closed in April.Meanwhile, for Woody Johnson, the new purchase gives him a new foothold in Manhattan’s ultra-exclusive co-op market, following the sale of his Upper East Side duplex at 834 Fifth Avenue to billionaire Leonard Blavatnik for $77.5 million more than a decade ago. His other holdings include a Bedminster, New Jersey, estate that he bought in 1984 and a Palm Beach home acquired in 2020 for roughly $33 million. The Park Avenue purchase gives him a new base in the city.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: A Texas man said he inherited $35,000 from his father and used $70,000 from earlier accounts for his marital home; after divorce, a November 17 court upheld the property division because he could not trace the money
articles.summary: A Texas man who said he inherited $35,000 from his father and put another $70,000 from past savings toward the family home has lost his bid to have the
articles.body: A Texas man who said he inherited $35,000 from his father and put another $70,000 from past savings toward the family home has lost his bid to have the money counted as his own separate property after a divorce court battle. The Texas Fourteenth Court of Appeals backed the original property split on November 17, 2026. The court ruled that Julian Poole had not shown enough proof of where the money came from or how it was spent. Judges found that his word alone was not enough to overturn the legal rule that property held during a marriage belongs to both spouses. The ruling came in Julian Poole v. Alice Devon Poole, an appeal over how assets were split after the couple divorced in Fort Bend County, Texas. The appeals court decided that the trial judge acted fairly when dividing the couple's property and turning down Poole's request to treat several assets as his alone.Divorce dispute over marital assetsAccording to the court's written opinion, Julian Poole and Alice Devon Poole got married in January 1998. They had three children, and two of them were already adults by the time the divorce went to trial. Devon filed for divorce in March 2023. Julian filed a response three months later. Both wanted the court to recognize their own separate property and asked for a larger share of the shared marital assets. After a trial, the 387th District Court of Fort Bend County ended the marriage and split the couple's belongings. Each spouse got a 50 per cent share of the family home. Devon also received several bank accounts, retirement funds, and personal items. Julian was given multiple Capital One accounts, retirement investments, a 2017 Toyota Sienna, and other belongings. The trial judge did recognize two cars, a 1984 Porsche 911 and a 1985 Toyota Camry, as Julian's separate property because he bought them before the wedding. Devon's wedding ring was also confirmed as her own separate property. Julian appealed the split, arguing that the court had failed to count other assets that he believed belonged only to him.$35,000 inheritance lacked supporting recordsOne of Julian's main arguments centered on a $35,000 inheritance he said he got from his father's estate. During the trial, Julian's sister, Tania Arlinghaus, testified that their father died without a will. Their mother then set aside shares of the estate for the four children. Arlinghaus told the court she did not get cash directly because money from the estate paid for her college tuition instead. Julian testified that he received $35,000 from his father's estate. He wanted the court to treat that sum as his separate property rather than part of the shared marital assets. Still, the appeals court found that he failed to show proof of what happened to the cash after he got it. The opinion noted that he did not prove whether the inheritance went into a separate bank account or was used to buy a specific asset or financial product.He also failed to hand over supporting records, such as probate papers or bank deposit slips, that could verify where the money came from and where it went. The judges concluded that his own testimony about getting the money was the only proof backing his claim. Because of that, the court saw no reason to overturn the trial judge's refusal to count the $35,000 as his separate property.$70,000 home deposit also came under scrutinyAnother major part of the fight involved roughly $70,000 that Julian said he put toward the down payment on the couple's home. He testified that he opened a Capital One account before marrying Devon in 1998. However, he admitted that more money was put into the account while they were married. When asked about the account's starting balance, Julian said he could not recall the exact figure. He also pointed to money from other bank accounts, certificates of deposit, and cash from selling two Porsche cars.During his testimony, he said: "My testimony is, that was 30 years ago. I’m not 100 percent. But I believe it was 100,000 and I was going to settle on 70 to be generous. I have proof of a CD of, you know, 20, sorry."He also mentioned other savings, including bank accounts and certificates of deposit. Yet the court found that he never submitted paper records to back up those claims. There were no records showing what the Capital One account held when the marriage started, how much went in or out during the marriage, or its balance right before the trial. The judges also pointed out that Julian admitted adding money to the account during the marriage without showing which dollars were his own and which came from marital paychecks. The couple bought their home roughly ten years after their wedding. According to the court, the lack of bank records made it impossible to prove that the $70,000 down payment came strictly from Julian's separate money.Texas law requires clear financial tracingThe appeals court explained that Texas law separates individual property from shared marital property. Under the Texas Family Code, assets owned before marriage, along with gifts or inheritances received during marriage, can count as separate property. However, the law also assumes that anything owned by either spouse during a marriage or at divorce belongs to both of them together. A spouse who wants to challenge that rule must track and prove the separate property using clear and convincing evidence.The court pointed to past rulings showing that paper records, like bank statements and business files, help prove where cash started and how it moved between accounts. It also noted the legal rule that when personal and marital funds are mixed in one bank account, marital funds are generally assumed to be spent first. In Julian's case, the judges found that he failed to prove the account's financial history. As a result, the money could not be reliably identified as his separate property.The court also reviewed his request to be paid back for the $70,000 he said went toward the family home. It explained that repayment may be granted when one spouse's separate estate pays for something that benefits the shared marital estate without getting equal value back. Still, the person asking for repayment must prove the spending, the value added, and the legal reason for getting paid back. Julian offered no records showing what share of the down payment came from his own separate funds. The court therefore turned down his repayment request as well.Appeal also covered child support and legal representationJulian brought up several other complaints in his appeal, including claims of poor legal representation, mishandled evidence, and mistakes in how child support was figured. He also challenged the original parenting schedule. The appeals court rejected his claim of poor legal representation, explaining that this legal argument does not apply to divorce cases under Texas law. His complaints about child custody and visitation could no longer be reviewed because the youngest child turned 18 while the appeal was underway.On child support, the trial judge had ordered Julian to pay $866 a month. The appellate opinion noted that Devon had presented records using his income and the Texas Attorney General's 2024 tax charts to calculate a monthly payment of $866.28. Julian did not object to those figures during the trial. The appeals judges saw no valid reason to change that payment order. They also turned down his complaints about evidence that was never officially entered during the trial, noting that he failed to raise those objections properly at the time.Court leaves original property division intactIn its November 17 ruling, the Texas Fourteenth Court of Appeals rejected Julian's arguments and upheld the trial court's decision. The ruling did not say that the inheritance or earlier savings never existed. Instead, it found that Julian failed to provide the paper records needed to prove their separate status under Texas law. In the end, the case came down to the difference between claiming money belongs to one spouse and proving its financial trail with hard records.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Building weapons of tomorrow: Why China is desperate for Nvidia AI chips
articles.summary: China is looking to get its hands on some of America's most powerful artificial intelligence chips to build the weapons of tomorrow, even as Washington
articles.body: China is looking to get its hands on some of America's most powerful artificial intelligence chips to build the weapons of tomorrow, even as Washington tightens its grip on semiconductor exports to Beijing.The Chinese military is seeking advanced Nvidia processors to accelerate its push towards AI-powered warfare, raising fresh concerns in Washington that American technology could end up strengthening one of its biggest military rivals.According to a report by Reuters, citing the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission's annual report, Beijing is seeking ways to access advanced computing technology despite US export restrictions.China's military modernisation is increasingly centred on integrating artificial intelligence into its battlefield operations. Beijing has been pursuing a military strategy often described as intelligentized warfare, in which AI, big data, autonomous systems and advanced computing are used to improve the speed and effectiveness of military operations.The People's Liberation Army (PLA) is seeking to incorporate AI into several areas, including intelligence gathering, surveillance, target identification, weapons development and command-and-control systems. The objective is to process vast amounts of battlefield information, identify potential threats and accelerate military decision-making.Why China needs Nvidia chipsAt the centre of China's AI ambitions is the need for high-performance computing power, which is essential for training and running sophisticated artificial intelligence models.Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) are among the world's most advanced processors for such tasks, allowing computers to process enormous volumes of data and perform multiple calculations simultaneously.For the Chinese military, access to these processors could help accelerate the development of AI-enabled weapons, improve battlefield intelligence analysis and strengthen command-and-control systems. Advanced computing is also critical to developing autonomous military platforms and integrating AI into complex weapons systems.China has been developing its own AI processors, including Huawei's Ascend and Cambricon's Siyuan series. However, according to the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, these domestic chips continue to lag behind more advanced products from Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), leaving Beijing keen to access American semiconductor technology.US export restrictions on advanced Nvidia chipsWashington has been tightening restrictions on China's access to advanced American semiconductor technology since 2022, citing concerns that the processors could be used to strengthen Beijing's military capabilities.The latest move came on Monday, when the Trump administration announced further restrictions on China's access to advanced chips from companies including Nvidia. The measures are aimed at closing loopholes that could allow Chinese entities to obtain restricted computing capabilities despite Washington's export controls.Nvidia has said that US export restrictions have effectively shut it out of China's AI data-centre market. However, a Reuters review found more than $3 billion worth of Chinese computing projects using its restricted chips, highlighting the difficulties Washington faces in preventing access to American technology.Why AI is becoming critical to the future of warfareArtificial intelligence is increasingly becoming a force multiplier in modern warfare, allowing militaries to analyse battlefield information, identify enemy targets and make operational decisions at speeds beyond conventional human capabilities.AI can process data from satellites, drones, radar and surveillance networks, helping commanders respond faster to emerging threats.Paul Scharre, vice-president at the Center for a New American Security (CNAS) and a former US Army Ranger, has warned that future conflicts could involve thousands of autonomous drones operating together in coordinated swarms across air, land and sea. Such systems could fundamentally change how militaries conduct surveillance and attacks.The United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR) has also highlighted how AI is accelerating military operations by reducing the time between identifying a target and striking it.However, experts warn that excessive dependence on autonomous systems could reduce human oversight and increase the risk of miscalculations during conflicts.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump, JD Vance face scrutiny as incoming House Oversight chief targets 12 allies in sweeping new probes
articles.summary: The incoming Democratic chairman of the House Oversight Committee, Representative Robert Garcia, has launched the first steps towards a series of
articles.body: The incoming Democratic chairman of the House Oversight Committee, Representative Robert Garcia, has launched the first steps towards a series of investigations targeting US President Donald Trump, his family and key administration officials ahead of Democrats taking control of the House in the new Congress.Garcia, a Democrat from California, sent 12 document preservation letters on Wednesday, asking prominent figures in Trump's orbit to retain records and communications that could be relevant to the planned investigations. The recipients include Vice President JD Vance, Trump's sons Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, son-in-law Jared Kushner, former US ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller.According to The New York Post, the incoming committee chairman is preparing investigations into the Trump family's business dealings, alleged misconduct within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the federal government's handling of convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's case.Trump family's business dealings, immigration crackdown under scrutinyIn letters addressed to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, Democrats alleged that the president's family had benefited financially from his time in office."Oversight Democrats have been investigating the potential corruption, self-dealing, and abuses of power that have funnelled billions of dollars to the Trump family as Americans struggle with rising costs," the letters said.The lawmakers further alleged that the president's sons had pursued business interests that appeared to allow them to profit from their father's presidency.Miller was also among the recipients of the letters, with Democrats seeking accountability for alleged abuses linked to the Trump administration's mass deportation campaign.The letter accused officials of orchestrating, carrying out and covering up alleged misconduct within federal agencies. Democrats said they had heard accounts from people affected by the immigration crackdown as well as whistleblowers concerned about agency conduct.Other figures targeted include former Homeland Security secretary Kristi Noem, former DHS senior adviser Corey Lewandowski, former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, Attorney General Todd Blanche, Federal Bureau of Prisons Director William K Marshall III and Trust for the National Mall CEO Catherine Townsend.Garcia signals aggressive oversight agendaGarcia has indicated that Democrats intend to pursue an extensive investigative agenda when they assume control of the committee in the new Congress. He said the investigations would "lay the groundwork for legislation which helps all Americans".The incoming chairman had earlier warned Trump allies to "lawyer up" following Republicans' losses in the 2026 midterm elections. Democrats have also indicated that their investigations could extend to corporations and individuals associated with Epstein.The Oversight Committee could also play a central role if House Democrats pursue impeachment efforts during the next Congress. However, no formal impeachment proceedings have been launched against Trump through the committee.Trump and his family have repeatedly denied wrongdoing over their business interests. The president has also described the Democrats' investigative demands as "extortion at the highest level".Republicans, meanwhile, have accused Democrats of prioritising political retaliation over addressing issues such as the rising cost of living. While Noem and Miller faced criticism over the administration's immigration crackdown, most Republicans have continued to defend the White House's approach.It remains unclear whether the 12 recipients will comply with the requests to preserve their documents and communications.Republican Representative Jim Jordan of Ohio is expected to lead the party's opposition to the investigations in the new Congress. Representatives Brandon Gill and Pat Fallon, both Republicans from Texas, have expressed interest in becoming the ranking member of the House Oversight Committee.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump, Putin to hold talks in China after 2025 Alaska summit failed to end Ukraine war
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump will hold a separate meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin in China on Thursday.
articles.body: US president Donald Trump will hold a separate meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin in China on Thursday. This marks their first face-to-face talks since a 2025 summit in Alaska failed to produce an agreement to end Russia's war in Ukraine.A US official confirmed the planned meeting, which will take place ahead of an unprecedented trilateral engagement involving Trump, Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Trump has said he intends to discuss both the Ukraine war and nuclear weapons with the two leaders, raising the possibility of renewed efforts to negotiate an end to the conflict.Reports by Russian news agency IFX also suggested that Trump and Putin did not have a substantive conversation when they met briefly in China on Wednesday, and no full-scale bilateral talks between the two leaders are planned for Thursday. One hour has been allocated for the trilateral meeting between the leaders of Russia, the US and China.The Alaska meeting in August 2025 had raised hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough, but the talks ended without a deal. Since then, Trump has repeatedly expressed confidence that he could bring the war to an end, even as negotiations have struggled to make progress.This time, Trump has suggested that the scale of Russian military casualties could create an opening for an agreement. Speaking before his departure for Asia, he said he believed a settlement was close."I think it's very close to getting it done," Trump said on Tuesday. articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan walked out of Ghaziabad's Dasna jail on Wednesday after spending nearly a year behind bars, drawing a crowd of
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan walked out of Ghaziabad's Dasna jail on Wednesday after spending nearly a year behind bars, drawing a crowd of more than 600 supporters who had gathered outside the prison to welcome him. His sons, Abdullah Azam and Adeeb, were present to receive him. Adeeb described the occasion as Eid for the family, while Abdullah declared, "Tiger is back."Khan was released after the completion of formalities following the arrival of his release warrant at the jail around 4.30pm. Supporters greeted him with slogans of "Azam Khan Zindabad" as they surrounded his black SUV and competed to shake hands with him.However, he did not make any statement to the media and left for his residence in Rampur.Khan had been lodged in jail since November 17, 2025, in connection with a double PAN card case. Although he had briefly walked out of Rampur jail on October 31, he was immediately arrested by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in a separate case linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and the Jauhar Trust. He was subsequently shifted to Dasna jail.His latest release followed an interim bail order granted by the Allahabad high court.The ED approached the Supreme Court on Wednesday, challenging the relief and seeking an urgent hearing. However, the apex court declined the request for immediate consideration.During the proceedings, Justice Joymalya Bagchi reportedly questioned the urgency of the ED's plea, observing, "What is the hurry? The sky will not fall. Let him remain on interim bail." The matter is scheduled to be taken up on Friday.Sons say he will return to public lifeAbdullah Azam welcomed his father's release, saying, "Tiger is back." He claimed that his father had been implicated in false cases and said he would now return to public life.Asked whether Khan would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Adeeb said his father would definitely enter the electoral fray, adding that Khan himself would be better placed to announce his future political strategy.He also dismissed apprehensions about another arrest following the release, saying the family had no reason to fear.Khan's wife, Tazeen Fatima, also expressed relief, saying she had faith in God and the judicial system. She alleged that certain forces did not want her husband to be released and said the High Court had once again delivered justice.ED case linked to Jauhar UniversityThe ED's action against Khan is linked to its investigation into the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and the Jauhar Trust. The agency has been examining alleged diversion and misuse of government funds and construction material, land purchases, and the sources of funds used in developing the university.The ED has identified Rs 426.46 crore as alleged proceeds of crime. On October 28, it provisionally attached land and buildings belonging to the university, valued at the same amount.The agency had challenged the Allahabad High Court's interim bail order, arguing before the Supreme Court that the High Court had passed the order in haste without granting it adequate time to file a detailed response. The apex court declined to entertain the plea for an urgent hearing and listed the matter for Friday.Akhilesh Yadav alleges injustice to Azam and familySamajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav welcomed Khan's release, alleging that the government had subjected the senior party leader and his family to injustice over several years.He reiterated the party's stand that the cases registered against Khan were false and alleged that the government's actions were politically motivated.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: During WWII, Cpl. John Hartley filmed a message home from Burma; more than 70 years later, the daughter who never met him finally saw him speaking on screen
articles.summary: Discover the emotional story of Ann Alsop, who, over 70 years after her father's passing, views his WWII film message from Burma, unveiling family secrets and bridging generations.
articles.body: During the Second World War, messages from the front frequently took weeks to reach families in Britain. Letters offered a way to establish a little thread of continuity. But a series of short films provided a more visceral, tethered message. This gave families the chance to see servicemen speaking on screen, sending greetings and brief messages from across the world. These films, known as Calling Blighty, were shown at special screenings across the country, according to the Daily Mail. Decades later, hundreds of these recordings surfaced in rusting film cans with their messages still intact.A message from BurmaAccording to the Daily Mail, Corporal John Hartley had a daughter he wasn’t destined to meet. When his short message addressed to his family was recorded in Burma during the Second World War, Ann Alsop was not yet born. Fast forward to decades later, that surviving footage bridged a generational chasm, allowing her a poignant first encounter with her father, whom she never met.Hartley was among the British servicemen who took part in the Calling Blighty films. The recordings featured men serving in Burma, part of what became known as the Forgotten Army. It was a moniker that stuck because their campaign received less attention than the war in Europe. Each film contained short portraits of servicemen addressing people they had left behind. Hartley’s contribution was brief. Looking towards the camera, he reassured his family that he was well before signing off with the words: “I’m in the pink. Cheerio. Best of luck”. His message was addressed to his wife, Mildred, who was pregnant with Ann when he left for Burma. Hartley died in 1944, while serving on patrol in the Burmese jungle, according to the Daily Mail. After his death, Mildred chose not to keep his memory alive within the household. She changed Ann’s surname to that of her stepfather and discarded the Hartley photographs and letters in her possession. Subsequently, Ann was raised, the Daily Mail said, with little knowledge of her biological father.The discovery of the Calling Blighty recordings eventually gave her a reason to revisit the past. By then, Ann was in her seventies, retired from teaching and living in Sheffield. She was married to Gerald, with children and grandchildren of her own. An important part of her father’s history had survived through her uncle Eric, who had given her a separate collection of Hartley’s letters and photographs. These were among the few personal records she possessed. The newly recovered footage offered an altogether different communion: the chance to see her father in a motion picture.The recordings had been presumed lost for decades before a collection of film cans was discovered among deteriorating reels. Despite their condition, the films were playable. Lists found inside the cans identified the servicemen along with the names and addresses of their families in Britain.Unearthing these directories set in motion an effort to reunite surviving kin with their voices of the past. Channel 4’s documentary, Messages Home: Lost Films of the British Army, followed several families as they watched their recordings. Some had known about the films; others had never seen their relatives in wartime footage.A long-awaited goodbye For Ann, watching Hartley was the beginning of a search for answers about his death. Military historian Rob Lyman helped her investigate his service and death. According to his account, Hartley had been shot in the back of the shoulder by a Japanese sniper who was retreating. Ann also learned that his comrades had carried his body back to their base.The circumstances of his death affected her profoundly, having spent much of her life without knowing how her father perished. The historical information provided the missing chapter that had long eluded her family’s history.The documentary prompted Ann to visit Burma, where she visited the military cemetery containing Hartley’s grave. No one in her family had previously made the journey to his burial place. She wanted to see where he had been laid to rest. At the graveside, Ann spoke to her father. She expressed regret that they had never known one another and told him his life continued through her descendants.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Google co-founder Sergey Brin and his ex-wife Nicole Shanahan are trying to offload their Malibu home.
articles.body: Google co-founder Sergey Brin and his ex-wife Nicole Shanahan are trying to offload their Malibu home. The former couple have listed the five-bedroom home for $33.5 million, according to Realtor.com. The listing is held by Michael Cunningham of Pinnacle Estate Properties. The sale listing comes less than five months after they listed it as a ‘summer rental’ for $175,000 a month.A house with famous ownersThe Malibu house, with ocean views and its own beach access, has had more than one A-list owner. In 2010, pop singer Pink bought the home for $11.9 million and lived there until 2016. She sold it for $12.5 million. Sergey Brin and Nicole Shanahan bought the house for $13.5 million in September 2020. About a year later, the couple parted ways, ending their three-year marriage. In May, the house was listed for rent at $175,000 a month. After offering the house as a luxury summer rental, the former couple have finally decided to sell it.The house is currently registered to a limited liability company in Nevada, according to property records. Shanahan’s family office manages the company. The LLC uses the same mailing address as her charity, the Bia-Echo Foundation, which is named after the couple’s daughter, Echo. Whether Shanahan ever lived in this Malibu home is unclear. Earlier, while speaking to Frontier Magazine, she revealed that she was living at a mountaintop ranch in California with her partner, Jacob Strumwasser.Inside the estateThe Malibu home, with breathtaking ocean views, has five bedrooms and 7.5 bathrooms. The gated entrance leads to a long driveway. The 1.2-acre lot is described as a ‘secluded sanctuary’ in the listing on Pinnacle Estate, surrounded by mature trees, lush landscaping and beautiful ocean views. Owners have keyed access to Little Dume Beach, a spot known for surfing. The newly completed estate is ‘a masterful expression of understated elegance, exceptional craftsmanship and Malibu's coveted “quiet luxury” lifestyle’, according to the listing.Inside, a curved ceiling tops the living room, and a fireplace sits in the corner. The primary suite is upstairs and comes with a sitting area offering serene treetop and ocean views. ‘A spa-inspired bathroom, multiple closets and beautifully appointed dressing areas are thoughtfully positioned to create an exceptional sense of privacy and tranquillity’, the listing says. The kitchen has a curved island and French doors that open onto a private deck. A second kitchen with its own stove sits at the back.The main floor also has a media room, which the listing says could become an office or library, and a gym with a wellness suite. A separate apartment with a private entrance includes another bedroom, its own kitchen and a living room. The listing also says the house uses building materials and systems designed to support wellness. The grounds include a pool with a large spa and a pagoda-style area for shade.Meanwhile, Sergey Brin’s real estate portfolio is quite impressive. He bought another Malibu home for $35 million in April 2022, about a mile from this one. articles.title: Bruce Springsteen’s archive began as a fan collection in 2001; 25 years later, a $50 million, 32,000-square-foot New Jersey music centre is open to the public and preserves more than 48,000 items
articles.summary: Bruce Springsteen’s archive began in 2001 as a fan collection, and 25 years later it has become a public destination in New Jersey.
articles.body: Bruce Springsteen’s archive began in 2001 as a fan collection, and 25 years later it has become a public destination in New Jersey. The Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music opened at Monmouth University on June 13, bringing together more than 48,000 artifacts and items in a $50 million, 32,000 square foot facility, according to Springsteen’s official site and Monmouth University’s Outlook.The centre is more than a museum dedicated to one artist. It explores the broader history of American music, with exhibits spanning country, classical, hip hop, sacred, and folk traditions, while also preserving Springsteen’s career and cultural influence.How the archive beganThe collection started in 2001 as a fan gathering project. Over the years, it grew into a serious archive of Springsteen’s work, including recordings, memorabilia, and materials connected to his career.That growth eventually required a permanent home. The centre now serves as the repository for Springsteen’s work while also expanding into a wider study of American music.The transition from a fan collection to a public institution reflects how music can become part of a larger cultural record. What began as a way to preserve one artist’s legacy has become a resource for students, researchers, and visitors.What visitors can seeAbout 20,000 square feet of the building are dedicated to exhibits. The centre features Springsteen related displays alongside rotating exhibitions that change roughly two to three times a year.The inaugural rotating exhibit, “Chimes of Freedom: Protest, Patriotism, and the Power of Song,” looks at protest music throughout American history. It includes artifacts dating back to the American Revolutionary War, including fifes from 1775 to 1783.The collection also includes more recent pieces, such as stage outfits worn by Chappell Roan and Sabrina Carpenter, along with a jacket worn by Elvis Presley. Some artifacts are on loan from other museums and collections, including Hard Rock.Interactive exhibits bring music to lifeThe centre uses more than static displays to engage visitors. Interactive exhibits allow people to play instruments and learn from members of the E Street Band through video.Other exhibits use headphones, video, lighting, and audiovisual elements to create a more immersive experience. Visitors can move through the space and encounter music in ways that feel personal rather than distant.One room recreates the atmosphere of a Springsteen concert. A projector plays concert footage while concert style lighting surrounds visitors, and the walls feature a photograph taken from the pit at one of his shows.A film narrated by SpringsteenThe centre also includes a theater where visitors can watch an approximately 25 minute film narrated by Springsteen. The film explores the influences of American music on his career and features locations significant to his history, including the Stone Pony and Asbury Park Convention Hall.The Wonder Bar was transformed to resemble the Freehold Cafe for the film. In it, Springsteen reflects on the influences that shaped his music and his early interest in performing.The film ends with an invitation to become a student of American music. That message captures the centre’s broader goal of helping visitors see music as a way to understand history.A building shaped by New JerseyThe centre’s design incorporates elements of New Jersey and Springsteen’s career. A boardwalk style pathway leads visitors to the building, referencing the Jersey Shore’s influence on his music.The building’s exterior has a rusted industrial appearance inspired by the industrial areas of New Jersey where Springsteen grew up. The design connects the physical space to the places and experiences that shaped his work.Springsteen related exhibits are located on the second floor and include artifacts from the 1970s through the present. This arrangement gives visitors a sense of how his career has evolved over time.Why the centre mattersThe centre is not just a tribute to Springsteen. It is also a resource for Monmouth students, who can visit for free with a reserved ticket. Faculty members can bring classes to use the collections and exhibits in coursework.The centre also offers student positions in its archives and store. It hosts events in addition to exhibits, including album release shows and other programming.For visitors, the appeal is personal. Some may come for Springsteen, while others may find connections to their own musical memories. The centre’s mission is to make that connection possible through artifacts, stories, and interactive experiences.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'It's the babies': Muslims projected to outnumber Christians by 2035, says Pew study
articles.summary: Muslims are projected to become the world's largest religious group by 2035, overtaking Christians, largely because of higher birth rates, according to
articles.body: Muslims are projected to become the world's largest religious group by 2035, overtaking Christians, largely because of higher birth rates, according to new projections by the Pew Research Center.The study, which examines changes in the size of major religious groups between 2020 and 2070, found that both Islam and Christianity are growing. However, the Muslim population is expanding at a much faster pace, driven mainly by higher fertility rates and a younger population.“It's the babies,” said Pew senior demographer Conrad Hackett, explaining that conversion and other changes in religious identity play a much smaller role in the growth of the Muslim population than birth rates.According to Pew, Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children during 2020-2025, compared with 2.5 among Christian women. The average for women belonging to other religious groups was 1.6, below the replacement level of 2.1 children per woman.Pew estimates that the world had 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims in 2020. By 2035, the Muslim population is projected to reach 2.57 billion, compared with 2.52 billion Christians.If current trends continue, the gap is expected to widen further. By 2070, the number of Muslims worldwide is projected to exceed 3.6 billion, while the Christian population is expected to remain just below 3 billion.The projections take into account differences in the age profiles and fertility rates of religious groups, as well as patterns of religious switching and migration.The world's population is expected to grow by 29% between 2020 and 2070. Muslims and Christians are the only major religious groups projected to grow at or above that pace, with their populations expected to increase by 80% and 30%, respectively.Hindus & Jews are projected to declineHindus and Jews are also projected to grow in absolute numbers, but their share of the global population is expected to decline. The Buddhist population, meanwhile, is projected to shrink both in numbers and as a proportion of the world's population, partly because of expected population declines in China, South Korea and Japan.Much of the world's population growth over the coming decades is expected to take place in sub-Saharan Africa, where Christianity and Islam are the two major religions.Higher fertility rates and rising life expectancy in the region are expected to contribute to the growth of both communities.By 2070, more than half of the world's Christians are projected to live in sub-Saharan Africa. The Democratic Republic of Congo is expected to overtake the United States as the country with the largest Christian population, with its Christian population projected to triple to 270 million.In contrast, Europe's population is expected to decline by 17% by 2070. The number of Christians in the region is projected to fall by about a third, from 505 million in 2020 to 324 million. Over the same period, the Muslim share of Europe's population is expected to rise from 6% to 13%.Christians projected to lose majority in US, CanadaThe study also projects a decline in the Christian share of the population in the United States and Canada, alongside a rise in the number of people who identify as having no religious affiliation.Christians currently make up 62% of the US population. Pew projects that their share will fall below 50% by 2065. The number of Christians in the country is also expected to decline, from around 217 million in 2020 to about 174 million by 2070.In Canada, Christians are projected to account for less than half the population by 2030. By 2070, people with no religious affiliation are expected to outnumber Christians in the country.The unaffiliated group, often referred to as “nones”, includes atheists, agnostics and people who do not identify with any religion.Excluding China, where the unaffiliated population is already large but the overall population is expected to decline, the number of “nones” elsewhere is projected to increase by more than 180 million by 2070.They already make up a majority of the population in 10 countries, including the Czech Republic, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Uruguay and Vietnam. South Korea, France and the United Kingdom are projected to join that group by 2070.Pak projected to have world's largest Muslim populationPew estimates that Muslim mothers gave birth to around 252 million babies between 2020 and 2025, compared with 208 million born to Christian mothers.Muslims are the only major religious group projected to see the number of births continue to rise in the coming decades. Births among other groups are expected to remain broadly stable or gradually decline.By 2070, Pakistan is projected to have the world's largest Muslim population, followed by India, Nigeria and Indonesia. Indonesia currently has the largest Muslim population.Researchers said the projected changes underline the importance of understanding relations between religious communities.Gina Zurlo, a senior researcher at Harvard Divinity School who specialises in religious demographics, described Christian-Muslim relations as “extremely important” in light of the changing religious landscape.“The clash of civilization' theory still looms large in some religious communities and there is a lot of misunderstanding of both religions from both sides,” she told the Associated Press via email.“Many Christians are not happy to see that Islam will be the world's largest religion and it's causing even more angst.” “I hope people seek opportunities for greater interreligious education,” she added.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pearl Harbor survivor Gebhard Galle, who rescued four sailors from sinking ship, dies at 105
articles.summary: Gebhard “Geb” Galle, one of the few remaining survivors of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor who later risked his life to rescue four fellow sailors
articles.body: Gebhard “Geb” Galle, one of the few remaining survivors of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor who later risked his life to rescue four fellow sailors from a sinking US Navy ship during World War II, has died at the age of 105.Galle died on Saturday at his home in Moses Lake, Washington, the Pacific Historic Parks said. His death came on the same day as that of Freeman Johnson, 106, believed to be the oldest surviving veteran of the December 7, 1941, attack. According to the Associated Press, nearly a dozen Pearl Harbor survivors are believed to be still alive.Galle witnessed the Pearl Harbor attack aboard USS NevadaBorn in Germany, Galle moved with his family to North Dakota in 1928, when he was seven. He joined the US Navy in 1939 and was serving as a machinist’s mate aboard the battleship USS Nevada when Japanese forces attacked Pearl Harbor.On December 7, 1941, the 20-year-old sailor was below deck, waiting to be taken ashore for church services, when he spotted approaching aircraft through a porthole. He rushed to his battle station in the ship’s engineering section.The Nevada was struck by a torpedo and several bombs, causing flooding and fires. Although the crew managed to get the vessel moving, it eventually ran aground.Galle later recalled seeing the destruction after reaching the deck, including the capsized USS Oklahoma and the partially submerged USS Arizona. He described the scene as “a pretty sad lookout” in an interview with the Columbia Basin Herald in 2020.Defied order to rescue four sailors from sinking shipAfter the Pearl Harbor attack, Galle was assigned to the USS Northampton. The heavy cruiser came under attack from Japanese torpedoes during the Battle of Tassafaronga near Guadalcanal on November 30, 1942.As the ship began sinking, Galle was ordered to close a hatch behind four sailors, which would have left them trapped. However, he disobeyed the instruction and opened the hatch, allowing all four men to escape before securing it.The Northampton sank, leaving Galle and around 40 other sailors stranded in life rafts for more than a day before they were rescued, according to accounts of the battle.He later served aboard the USS Mobile and remained in the Navy until 1946.Honoured at Pearl Harbor anniversary ceremonyGalle attended a ceremony at Pearl Harbor in December 2016 marking the 75th anniversary of the attack and honouring those who served aboard the USS Nevada. Seventy-six sailors and Marines died as a result of the attack on the vessel, according to the US Navy.Speaking at the event, Galle said he did not hold hatred towards the Japanese people, saying that their wartime leader had led them astray.“We’re at peace now and I feel comfortable. I have no qualm. We’re all good people,” he said.After the war, Galle married and established a refrigeration and air-conditioning business in North Dakota. He later worked as a civil engineer with the US Air Force and the Army Corps of Engineers before retiring in the 1980s.In a letter marking Galle’s 104th birthday in 2025, then-Acting Chief of Naval Operations Admiral James Kilby praised his courage and selfless actions, describing them as an example of Navy valour.You use AI every day.
